- Phase 113V.N — Phase Finalization Notification Repair. Governance/notification repair phase, closing the "notification asymmetry" 113S/113T/113U/113V each documented and re-confirmed without repairing. Forensic finding 1: `pcae skill invoke phase-finalization <phase-id>` is Phase 64B.5's generic, read-only "Skill Invocation Targeting" preview (`build_skill_invocation_targeting()`) -- it never imports `notifications.py`, never constructs a `TelegramSink`, never reads `PCAE_NOTIFY_ENABLED`, and is not part of the real dispatch path at all. Forensic finding 2: its `target_unresolved`/`target_type_unresolved` failures came from `_sit_resolve_phase_target()` matching only against `_CRI_KNOWN_PHASES`, a hard-coded roadmap registry last extended around Phase 69P/64B.6E -- confirmed live that `pcae skill invoke phase-finalization 113D` (an entirely ordinary phase) fails identically to `113T`/`113U`/`113V`; "special" phase-ID shapes were never the actual variable. Forensic finding 3 (the real functional gap): `pcae phase complete` had no notification-dispatch idempotency guard, unlike `pcae task finish --commit`, which already carried a private marker-file workaround (with its own comment recording that `finalize_phase_report()` writes the report before attempting dispatch, so `PhaseReport.notification_result` can never itself answer "already sent" at decision time) -- re-running `pcae phase complete` for the same phase_id + commit could dispatch a duplicate Telegram final report. Repair: `_sit_resolve_phase_target()`/`_sit_infer_target_type()` (`src/pcae/core/agent.py`) now fall back to live repository state (`latest.json`, historical timestamped reports, quarantined reports, in-flight `.pcae/phase-completion-metadata.json`, PROJECT_STATUS.md's Current Phase line) before giving up, and classify any phase-shaped ID via a new grammar (`^\d+[A-Za-z]*(?:\.\d+)*(?:\.[A-Za-z]+)?$` -- normal `113D`, multi-letter-suffix `113XR`, dotted-numeric-subphase `113X.2`, dotted-letter-repair-suffix `113D.R`/`113V.N`) as `target_type=phase` even when nothing resolves it, so an unresolved phase gets a specific reason naming every source checked, and a syntactically invalid ID (reachable via explicit `--target-type phase`) is reported as a distinct `invalid_phase_id_form` signal rather than the generic `target_unresolved`. A new `notification_dispatch_note`, populated only for `invoke_skill_id="phase-finalization"`, states explicitly that the command never gates or reflects Telegram dispatch and points at `pcae notify status`/`pcae phase complete`/`pcae notify send-report --latest` instead. `pcae task finish --commit`'s marker-file idempotency logic (`.pcae/phase-reports/.last-notified.json`) is generalized into three shared `src/pcae/core/phase_reports.py` functions (`read_notification_dispatch_marker()`, `phase_already_notified(phase_id, commit_hash)`, `write_notification_dispatch_marker(phase_id, commit_hash)`); `task.py` is refactored to call them (behavior unchanged), and `pcae phase complete`'s `_finalize_report_and_notify()` (`src/pcae/commands/phase.py`) gains the same guard it previously lacked -- before dispatch it checks the marker; if already dispatched for this exact phase_id + commit, `PCAE_NOTIFY_ENABLED` is transparently suppressed for that call only and the printed outcome reads `Notification dispatch: skipped (idempotent — already dispatched)` with an explicit reason, never the generic "not enabled" message; after a real send succeeds the marker is written; a genuinely new commit for the same phase_id (e.g. a report-repair follow-up) is still treated as not-yet-dispatched and sent normally. `pcae notify send-report --latest` (the fully manual resend command) is deliberately left unguarded, since the phase-finalization skill's own documented workflow explicitly calls for resending Telegram after a report repair -- a legitimate, human-invoked, intentional resend, not an accidental duplicate. 18 new focused tests (`tests/test_phase_113v_n_notification_finalization_repair.py`): live-report-based resolution for normal/multi-letter/dotted/repair-suffix phase IDs, a quarantine-only phase resolving as `blocked` (not a clean target), grammar-invalid IDs rejected distinctly from not-found IDs, the `notification_dispatch_note`, the read-only preview's absence of dispatch side effects, the shared marker helpers' round-trip and non-matching-commit behavior, and end-to-end `pcae phase complete` idempotency (first call sends and writes the marker, second call for the same phase+commit is a no-op with an explicit reason, a new commit for the same phase still sends, and a missing `PCAE_NOTIFY_ENABLED` is reported accurately and never as `target_unresolved`). 5,674 pre-existing tests across `test_phase.py`/`test_task.py`/`test_phase_reports.py`/`test_phase_reports_cli.py`/`test_notifications.py`/`test_telegram_notifications.py`/`test_task_finish_notification_ordering.py`/`test_task_finish_report_trust_notification.py`/`test_phase_report_trust_gate.py`/`test_phase_report_trust_gate_cli.py`/`test_phase_report_trust_hard_fail.py`/`test_agent.py` (full skill-targeting suite)/`test_repository_transition_validator.py`/`test_finalization_notification_guarantee.py` all re-run clean; fast_green 4,390/4,390. - Phase 113S — Repository Transition Validator Architecture. Architecture/design only, no implementation -- turns the 113X/Claude-DeepSeek cross-agent incident (Phase 113D's canonical report carrying stale commits/test_results because a metadata file was never rewritten between phases) into a formal PCAE design principle: Model proposes, PCAE validates, repository advances only through valid state transitions; PCAE does not trust the intelligence of the agent, it trusts only repository state that satisfies continuously verified engineering invariants. Defines Repository State (14 independently-observable components -- git state, working tree, active task, phase identity, project status, phase reports, phase-completion metadata, architecture status, test results, governance checks, notification state, push state, runtime state, execution availability -- each with exactly one authoritative reader, never derived from another's free text); Proposed Transition (10 kinds: `start_task`, `modify_files`, `run_validation`, `commit`, `finish_task`, `complete_phase`, `push`, `notify`, `update_status`, `produce_report`); the Transition Validator itself (`validate_transition(current_state, proposed, target_state, invariants) -> TransitionVerdict`, a pure function with no field for proposing-agent identity); 15 invariant families (phase identity consistency, active task consistency, allowed file scope, commit lineage, report completeness, report trust, metadata consistency, architecture status consistency, recommended-next-phase consistency, test result consistency, push state consistency, notification eligibility, single-final-notification, no-execution-availability-unless-explicitly-enabled-by-future-contract, no-canonical-artifact-promotion-when-blocked); Accept/Reject/Quarantine/Requires-Human-Review semantics (exhaustive, mutually exclusive); a 5-state canonical artifact promotion model (Draft -> Blocked/Quarantined/Certified -> Canonical/latest, only Certified artifacts may ever become canonical); Notification eligibility (finalized + certified + push-clean + not-already-dispatched + transport configured/enabled, all simultaneously; intermediate reports never externally dispatched); the semantic/structural boundary (models own code design, implementation strategy, explanations, remediation, prose; PCAE owns identity, lifecycle, scope, reports, commits, pushes, notifications, canonical state); model-agnostic behavior (identical invariants for Claude, Claude-DeepSeek, Codex, Qwen, human operators, and future models -- the validator's signature has no field to plumb a different outcome by authorship); and future integration points (task lifecycle, phase lifecycle, commit governance, push governance, notification runtime, Runtime Snapshot/Advisory Runtime, future intent/approval/execution layers) documented without requiring redesign of any existing code path. Explicitly does not replace or modify `validate_finalization_gate()`, `validate_phase_identity()`, `check_task_zone_scope()`/`check_task_file_scope()`, or `pcae push check` -- describes them as specific, already-implemented instances of the general validator model. No source file under `src/pcae/` touched. 97 new documentation-completeness tests (`tests/test_repository_transition_validator_architecture.py`), all passing -- no implementation tests, since no implementation exists. Added `docs/PCAE_REPOSITORY_TRANSITION_VALIDATOR.md`, `docs/PHASE_113_REPOSITORY_TRANSITION_VALIDATOR_ARCHITECTURE.md`. Execution capability remains unavailable. Recommended next phase: 113T — Repository Transition Validator Contract Freeze.

- Phase 113D.R — Advisory Runtime Verification Report Repair. Corrective phase repairing the invalid canonical completion/report state left by Phase 113D -- not new development, no redo of 113D's implementation (independently verified present and correctly scoped), no Advisory Runtime/Runtime Snapshot/Runtime Context/Permission Broker/execution/authorization/plugin/Telegram-inbound/REST/Web-UI/reporting-architecture changes. Independent forensic verification had rejected 113D's canonical report because `.pcae/phase-completion-metadata.json` was never rewritten before 113D's `pcae phase complete` ran: `commits` carried Phase 113B's stale hashes (`d49351d5`, `8ec96882`) instead of 113D's real commit (`335e0c06`), `test_results` were byte-identical to 113B's own stale metadata (contradicting the report's own prose, which correctly acknowledged pre-existing failures), and `recommended_next_phase` was empty despite prose/Architecture Status both saying 113R -- `pcae push check` independently confirmed `Phase report trust: failed`, `Missing fields: recommended_next_phase`. Repair: `commits` now references the real 113D commit; `recommended_next_phase` populated as `113R — Advisory Runtime Architecture Review`; `test_results` independently re-run against current repository state rather than copied from any prior report -- focused 124/124 (`test_advisory_runtime_verification.py` + `test_advisory_runtime.py`), advisory/runtime broader group 1218/1218, release/lifecycle regression 1036/1039 (3 pre-existing failures, 2 reconfirmed already failing at pre-113D commit `1a502fc3`, the 3rd a test-isolation fragility unmasked by Current Phase returning to a normal single-letter shape -- none are 113D regressions), `fast_green` 4389/4390 (1 pre-existing state-dependent failure, task idle), full suite 16338/16341. `pcae push check` now reports the report as trusted. Recommended next phase: 113R — Advisory Runtime Architecture Review.

- Phase 113D — Advisory Runtime Verification & Compatibility. Verification and hardening of the Advisory Runtime prototype (113C) against the architecture (113A) and contracts (113B). Verification/compatibility only — no new advisory behavior, no execution, no authorization, no Permission Broker enforcement. All 12 verification areas confirmed: Advisory Runtime consumes Runtime Snapshot only, providers remain modular, results follow 113B contract, explainability is complete (all 8 facets), recommendations are reproducible from Runtime Snapshot, aggregation is deterministic, no provider inspects Runtime internals directly, no PermissionBroker.evaluate() is called, no plugin loading/invocation occurs, no mutation of Runtime Snapshot or Runtime Context, runtime state remains Observed, execution capability remains unavailable. 41 new verification tests (`tests/test_advisory_runtime_verification.py`), all passing; all 83 existing 113C tests continue to pass. Broader suites: 3671 runtime/contract/autonomy/plugin/advisory pass, 1532 task/phase/notifications pass (2 pre-existing failures unrelated), 4389 fast_green pass (1 pre-existing failure unrelated). Safety invariants all confirmed unchanged. Added `docs/PHASE_113_ADVISORY_RUNTIME_VERIFICATION.md`. Recommended next phase: 113R — Advisory Runtime Architecture Review.

- Phase 113XR — Governance Recovery Review. Final architectural review of the 113X governance-repair sequence (113X.1-113X.5) -- review/verification only, no new features, no Advisory Runtime changes, no execution capability. Re-verified every forensic finding directly against the current codebase and live CLI behavior rather than trusting prior phase reports: 5 live reproductions in an isolated scratch repository (finalization blocker → quarantined, never overwrites `latest.json`, exit non-zero; a summary mentioning three unrelated phase numbers at once → `phase_id` unaffected, stays the metadata-declared value; zero identity sources available → explicit fail-closed refusal, zero artifacts written; Architecture Status with only one phase in a series complete → no overclaim of later milestones; a finalized-but-partial completion with notifications enabled → labeled WARNING event actually dispatched, distinctly titled/severity-flagged, never resembling a normal completion). `git log` across the entire 113X commit range against every Advisory Runtime/Runtime Snapshot/Runtime Context/Runtime Registry/Runtime Inspect/Permission Broker file returns zero commits -- exactly 5 source files were touched across all five repair phases (`cli.py`, `commands/phase.py`, `commands/task.py`, `core/notifications.py`, `core/phase_reports.py`). Findings 1, 3, 4, 6, and 7 classified Resolved; the notification-guarantee gap and cross-agent-continuity concern classified Resolved; one new, minor, non-blocking observation recorded (`pcae phase complete` has no duplicate-notification idempotency guard, unlike `pcae task finish --commit`'s path -- not unsafe, not a 113X regression, just undocumented). `pcae session bootstrap`, `pcae runtime inspect`, and `pcae runtime inspect --json` all confirmed coherent and unchanged (Runtime state Observed, execution capability unavailable, maximum plugin capability observe). Recommendation: safe to resume the normal roadmap. Added `docs/PHASE_113_GOVERNANCE_RECOVERY_REVIEW.md`. Recommended next phase: 113D — Advisory Runtime Verification & Compatibility.

- Phase 113X.5 — Architecture Status Canonicalization. Governance repair phase, closing 113X (Cross-Agent Governance Verification) Finding 4 -- no Advisory Runtime/Runtime Snapshot/Runtime Context/Runtime Registry/Runtime Inspect/Permission Broker/execution/authorization/plugin/Telegram-inbound/REST/Web UI/Dashboard changes; no changes to Canonical Phase Identity, Finalization Gate, or Mobile Notification Guarantee. `_series_label()`'s hardcoded `SERIES_MAP` (e.g. `"113": "Advisory Runtime (Architecture, Contract, Prototype)"`) over-claimed completion the moment any one phase in a series completed, regardless of which specific phases actually had -- and the existing consistency check meant to catch this searched for the series digits as a literal substring inside the display label, which the hardcoded label never contained, so it could never fire. New `_render_series_milestone_label()` derives each series' label from exactly the phases whose own `"## Phase X Complete"` header exists, sorted deterministically by `(series, branch, subphase)` (independent of file section order -- closing Finding 6's latent recommendation-ordering fragility too): a single completed phase renders as its full title; multiple phases render as their titles' longest-common-prefix ("track name") plus each phase's own distinguishing remainder, joined with " + " -- so the label grows exactly in step with actual completion (only 113A → "Advisory Runtime Architecture"; +113B → "Advisory Runtime: Architecture + Contract Freeze"; +113C → "...+ Prototype (Observation-Only)"). New structured `completed_phase_ids` field lets consistency validation use direct set-membership instead of regex-parsing display labels -- the fragility that let Finding 4 go undetected. `validate_phase_identity()`'s Architecture Status checks rewritten around it, plus a new check that `current_runtime_state == "Observed"` can never coexist with `execution_availability != "unavailable"`. A "consecutive letters" gap-detection heuristic was prototyped and rejected: it produced a false positive against this repo's own real history (`111R` legitimately follows `111D` with a non-consecutive mnemonic letter) -- the underlying guarantee (never claim unearned work) is satisfied structurally instead, since the label renderer only ever includes evidenced phases. `recommended`/"planned" now preferentially reads the "Recommended next repo phase" sentence from within the "## Current Phase" section's own bounded text rather than "nearest the top of the whole file." 15 new tests (`tests/test_architecture_status_canonicalization.py`); 1 pre-existing test in `tests/test_phase_identity.py` strengthened from a soft to a strict assertion. Added `docs/PHASE_113X5_ARCHITECTURE_STATUS_CANONICALIZATION.md`, including an architectural review recommending Architecture Status remain inside the report generator (single consumer, pure function of already-canonical read-only sources) rather than become a dedicated Runtime Service, with the extraction path documented for if/when a second independent consumer appears.

- Phase 113X.4 — Canonical Phase Identity Repair. Governance repair phase, closing 113X (Cross-Agent Governance Verification) Finding 3 in full -- no Advisory Runtime/Runtime Snapshot/Runtime Context/Runtime Registry/Runtime Inspect/Permission Broker/execution/authorization/plugin/Telegram-inbound/REST/Web UI/Dashboard/Architecture-Status changes. 113X.2 only detected a *disagreement* between a regex-derived `--summary` phase_id and metadata's declared one; this phase removes the regex derivation itself. New `resolve_canonical_phase_identity()` (`src/pcae/core/phase_reports.py`) never takes a summary parameter at all, resolving `phase_id`/`phase_name` from exactly one source in precedence order -- active task contract (`Title` field, anchored "Phase X: ..." parse), explicit phase-completion metadata (structured fields, never regex), active lifecycle context (PROJECT_STATUS.md's Current Phase, only if not marked completed), explicit `--phase-id`/`--phase-name` CLI argument (new flags on `pcae phase complete`) -- never free text. Fails closed (refuses finalization, writes nothing at all, not even quarantined) if none resolve. `recommended_next_phase` similarly drops its `_derive_next_phase(summary)` fallback -- an absent structured value now fails closed via the pre-existing `validate_finalization_gate()` blocker instead of parsing prose. `_derive_phase_id()`/`_derive_phase_name()`/`_derive_next_phase()` and `resolve_finalization_phase_identity()` (113X.2) removed as dead/superseded code. Also removed `validate_phase_identity()`'s check #5 ("Summary text vs report phase_id"), discovered while writing this phase's own mandated regression tests to itself be a form of free-text influence over finalization outcomes, contradicting the phase's own objective. 27 new tests (`tests/test_canonical_phase_identity_source_repair.py`, superseding `tests/test_canonical_phase_identity_repair.py`); 2 pre-existing tests updated in `tests/test_phase_identity.py` and 1 in `tests/test_finalization_notification_guarantee.py` (113X.2's "conflict" scenario is now "metadata wins cleanly," not a conflict). Added `docs/PHASE_113X4_CANONICAL_PHASE_IDENTITY_REPAIR.md`. Numbered 113X.4 rather than the requested "113X.2" since 113X.2 and 113X.3 were already completed in this arc; recreating that number would itself be the phase-identity collision this arc exists to prevent (confirmed with the human operator before starting).

- Phase 113X.3 — Finalized Phase Mobile Notification Guarantee. Governance repair phase, closing a problem 113X.2's own completion exposed — no Advisory Runtime changes, no execution. Two distinct bugs: (1) a naive lexicographic "backward-pointing recommended next phase" heuristic (in both `commands/phase.py` and `_check_canonical_metadata_consistency()`) compared phase IDs as strings, wrongly flagging `"113D"` as before `"113X.2"` (`'D' < 'X'`), forcing 113X.2's own completion through `--allow-partial-report` and leaving it `partial`; (2) once a report was `partial`, `pcae phase complete` cleared `PCAE_NOTIFY_ENABLED` before calling `finalize_phase_report()`, suppressing *all* notification even though canonical `latest.md`/`latest.json` had still been written — the operator received no Telegram signal at all for a finalized, pushed phase. New `is_phase_id_backward()`/`_parse_phase_id_shape()` make phase-ID comparison branch-aware: two IDs are only orderable when they share a series and are both on the lettered mainline or both on the `"X"` exceptional branch; different branch kinds are never flagged backward. New notification-outcome model (`NOTIFICATION_OUTCOME_ATTEMPTED`/`_SENT`/`_SKIPPED_WITH_REASON`/`_FAILED_WITH_REASON`, `_classify_notification_outcome()`) always recorded on `finalize_phase_report()`'s return value and `report.notification_result`. `finalize_phase_report()` gains `report_is_complete:`/`report_incomplete_reason:` parameters (default `None`, exactly preserving prior behavior for callers that don't pass them, notably `pcae task finish --commit`): when explicitly `False`, a distinctly different, clearly-labeled WARNING event (`phase_report_to_partial_warning_notification_event()`, new in `core/notifications.py` — title "PHASE FINALIZED BUT REPORT PARTIAL — mobile operator attention required", forced `SEVERITY_WARNING`) is dispatched instead of the normal "Phase COMPLETED" one and instead of silence — 105D's rule that partial reports are never sent as *normal* final reports is preserved by construction (a different event, not a suppressed one). Blocked/quarantined reports (113X.1) remain fully silent, unchanged — the guarantee applies only when canonical artifacts are actually updated, matching the brief's own scoping and avoiding weakening quarantine semantics. Removed the now-dead `PCAE_NOTIFY_ENABLED`-clearing suppression hack and `_notification_skip_reason()` helper from `commands/phase.py`. 17 new tests (`tests/test_finalization_notification_guarantee.py`); one pre-existing test updated (it asserted the exact old, now-intentionally-changed "always silent for partial" behavior). Added `docs/PHASE_113X3_FINALIZED_PHASE_MOBILE_NOTIFICATION_GUARANTEE.md`. Reconfirmed the three previously-documented pre-existing test fragilities remain unrelated; observed one additional likely xdist parallel-worker race (`test_project_state_no_repository_files_created`, passes in isolation) consistent with this codebase's own previously-documented parallel-safety issue class.

- Phase 113X.2 — Canonical Phase Identity Source Repair. Governance repair phase, closing the one remaining finding from the Phase 113X (Cross-Agent Governance Verification) forensic audit that 113X.1 did not address — no Advisory Runtime changes, no execution. `pcae phase complete`'s finalization path combines two independent phase-identity sources: the CLI/summary-derived `phase_id` and `.pcae/phase-completion-metadata.json`'s own declared `phase_id`. A mismatch between them was previously resolved silently (metadata discarded, console-only warning, finalization proceeded on git-derived fallback data) without ever becoming a `validate_finalization_gate()` blocker (113X audit Finding 3). New `resolve_finalization_phase_identity()` (`src/pcae/core/phase_reports.py`) is the single canonical resolution point for these two sources; `validate_finalization_gate()` gains an `identity_conflict:` parameter, appending a genuine conflict to the same blockers list `validate_phase_identity()` already populates, so it is enforced through 113X.1's existing quarantine path rather than a new mechanism. Every other identity-divergence point named in the brief (report body, canonical latest artifact, quarantine artifact, notification/report status, canonical-report-file vs current report) was found during inspection to already converge on a single value by construction, or to already feed the gate via `report_completeness`/`_check_canonical_metadata_consistency()`. 16 new tests (`tests/test_canonical_phase_identity_repair.py`). Added `docs/PHASE_113X2_CANONICAL_PHASE_IDENTITY_SOURCE_REPAIR.md`. Found (not fixed — pre-existing, out of scope, documented) three test fragilities in the full `python -m pytest` run, each reconfirmed via `git stash -u` against the clean pre-113X.2 baseline: the already-known `test_both_paths_agree_on_complete_report` (113X.1), plus `test_recommended_next_phase_matches_real_project_status` and `test_real_todo_not_flagged_stale_against_real_project_status`, both of which hardcode an expectation that PROJECT_STATUS.md's current recommended phase is still `"112C"`.

- Phase 113X.1 — Finalization Gate Enforcement Repair. Governance repair phase, scoped to Finding 1 of the Phase 113X (Cross-Agent Governance Verification) forensic audit — no Advisory Runtime changes, no execution. `validate_finalization_gate()` correctly detected phase-identity/trust blockers, but `finalize_phase_report()` wrote `latest.md`/`latest.json` unconditionally regardless of the gate result, so a blocked report could still become the canonical "latest" artifact with no persisted blocker evidence (reproduced directly against the repository's own pre-repair `.pcae/phase-reports/latest.json`, which `validate_phase_identity()` flags as blocked). `finalize_phase_report()` (`src/pcae/core/phase_reports.py`) gains an optional `gate:` parameter (default `None`, preserving prior unconditional-write behavior for every existing caller/test that doesn't pass it); when the caller passes a blocked gate, the report is written to a new quarantine path (`write_quarantined_report()`, under `.pcae/phase-reports/quarantine/`) instead of `latest.md`/`latest.json` or the normal timestamped filename, with the blocker list persisted directly inside the quarantined JSON/Markdown. `pcae phase complete` (`src/pcae/commands/phase.py`) now passes its already-computed gate through (except when `--allow-partial-report` is given, which keeps its pre-existing, tested override behavior unchanged — out of this repair's scope). `pcae task finish --commit`'s report-finalization path is deliberately unchanged: it is documented and tested as warning-only, writing partial/incomplete reports for human visibility during normal mid-workflow states (e.g. not yet pushed) — a different, legitimate case from Finding 1's actual concern (a report whose identity/claims are wrong). Because blocked reports never touch `latest.json`, `pcae push check`/report trust now can never read a quarantined artifact as the latest. 15 new tests (`tests/test_finalization_gate_enforcement.py`). Added `docs/PHASE_113X1_FINALIZATION_GATE_ENFORCEMENT_REPAIR.md`. Found (not fixed, out of scope, documented, left for 113X.2) one pre-existing test fragility: `tests/test_rc_audit_findings_repair.py::TestAsymmetryReproduction::test_both_paths_agree_on_complete_report` fails on a clean checkout because `validate_phase_identity()` reads the real `PROJECT_STATUS.md` rather than an isolated fixture. Recommended next phase: 113X.2 — Canonical Phase Identity Source Repair.

- Phase 113B.2 — Phase Identity & Lifecycle Hardening. Corrective governance hardening phase — no Advisory Runtime changes, no execution. Strengthens PCAE phase identity validation to prevent agents from silently drifting into the wrong phase. Added `validate_phase_identity()` to `src/pcae/core/phase_reports.py`: cross-references report phase_id against PROJECT_STATUS.md, Architecture Status, metadata execution integration status, summary text, and commit messages; integrated into `validate_finalization_gate()` as hard blockers. Added `_detect_phase_ambiguity()` to `src/pcae/core/context.py`: compares active task phase against PROJECT_STATUS.md current phase, detects completed-phase ambiguity in bootstrap with ⚠️ banner. Improved bootstrap prompt with explicit "Current phase" display and fail-closed resolution instructions. Fail-closed, sub-phase tolerant, backward compatible. 17 new tests (`tests/test_phase_identity.py`).

- Phase 113C — Advisory Runtime Prototype (Observation-Only). First implementation phase of the Advisory Runtime — introduces advisory reasoning only, no authorization, no execution, no enforcement. Implemented `src/pcae/core/advisory_runtime.py`: four frozen vocabulary tuples (`ADVISORY_CATEGORIES`, `SEVERITY_LEVELS`, `CONFIDENCE_LEVELS`, `ADVISORY_LIFECYCLE_STAGES`), `EvidenceReference` frozen dataclass (4 fields, validated at construction), `AdvisoryResult` frozen dataclass (14 fields matching 113B §1, `implementation_status` unconditionally `"execution_unavailable"` fail-closed), `ADVISORY_INVARIANT` module constant, `AdvisoryProvider` Protocol, four initial providers (`RuntimeHealthProvider` — 8 health-domain results, `GovernanceProvider` — 4 governance-domain results, `RuntimeContextProvider` — handles None context gracefully, `RegistryProvider` — 4–6 registry-domain results), deterministic aggregation pipeline (collect → normalize → deduplicate by fingerprint → sort by severity then category → assign stable `ADV-{category_slug}-{seq:04d}` IDs). All ten safety rules upheld. No CLI wiring, no execution capability, no mutation. Import surface limited to stdlib + `RuntimeSnapshot` (verified by AST-based import allowlist tests). Added `docs/PCAE_ADVISORY_RUNTIME_PROTOTYPE.md`, `docs/PHASE_113_ADVISORY_RUNTIME_PROTOTYPE.md`. 83 new tests (`tests/test_advisory_runtime.py`).

- Phase 113B — Advisory Runtime Contract Freeze. Contract/freeze phase only — no advisory implementation, no runtime behavior changes, no execution capability; no file under `src/pcae/` touched. Freezes the Advisory Runtime contracts (113A) before any advisory implementation begins. New principle: **Explainability precedes trust**. Freezes a fourteen-field `AdvisoryResult` contract (113A's nine extended by five: `source_snapshot_reference`, `reasoning_summary`, `alternative_considerations`, `remediation`, `implementation_status`; the brief's suggested `recommendation` field reconciled into 113A's existing `recommended_action` rather than duplicated), an eight-facet explainability contract plus a reproducibility principle (restating 110A §6's "Deterministic" Runtime Principle for Analysis specifically), a one-shape `EvidenceReference` evidence model (no evidence database, no audit persistence), advisory-category extension rules (open taxonomy, frozen meanings), severity/confidence semantics (four levels each, explicitly orthogonal, fail-closed ambiguity handling), a six-stage advisory lifecycle (contract only), a presentation contract (one model, many renderers), ten absolute safety rules (113A's seven plus deny/imply-approval/bypass-review-or-audit), and compatibility rules mirroring 112F's own discipline (no versioning field implemented this phase, consistent with 112F's own precedent). Added `docs/PCAE_ADVISORY_RUNTIME_CONTRACT.md`, `docs/PHASE_113_ADVISORY_RUNTIME_CONTRACT_FREEZE.md`. `docs/ROADMAP.md` evaluated, no change needed. 158 new tests (`tests/test_advisory_runtime_contract.py`), a pure documentation-verification suite.

- Phase 113A — Advisory Runtime Architecture. Architecture/design phase only — no advisory execution, no runtime behavior changes, no execution capability; no file under `src/pcae/` touched. First phase of the 113-series, following 112F's recommended "proceed" to Advisory Runtime work. Designs the Runtime subsystem responsible for producing read-only recommendations from Runtime Snapshot: analytical only, never executes, never authorizes, never mutates Runtime Context or Runtime Snapshot. New principle: **Recommendation precedes authorization**. Explicitly distinguished from this codebase's pre-existing, unrelated "IRG Challenge" advisory concept (strategic/roadmap review, not Runtime Snapshot analysis). Freezes a five-stage Advisory Pipeline (Runtime Snapshot → Analysis → Recommendation → Advisory Result → Presentation, no execution path at any stage), a nine-field Advisory Result model (architecture only: `advisory_id`, `category`, `severity` — new vocabulary distinct from `dry_run.py`'s enforcement-flavored `simulation_severity` — `confidence` — reuses this codebase's own existing capability-discovery vocabulary verbatim — `rationale`, `evidence_references`, `recommended_action`, `affected_runtime_objects`, `timestamp`), eight advisory categories as a deliberately open taxonomy (unlike 110B's closed ten-category plugin taxonomy), Runtime-Snapshot-only integration (no direct CLI/Telegram/REST dependency), a named-not-resolved plugin-integration gap (none of 110B's ten frozen plugin categories fits; no eleventh category added), a five-consumer presentation model (CLI, Telegram, REST, dashboard, AI agents; none implemented), and seven absolute safety rules. Added `docs/PCAE_ADVISORY_RUNTIME.md`, `docs/PHASE_113_ADVISORY_RUNTIME_ARCHITECTURE.md`. `docs/ROADMAP.md` evaluated, no change needed. 123 new tests (`tests/test_advisory_runtime_architecture.py`), a pure documentation-verification suite.

- Phase 112F — Runtime Snapshot Contract Freeze. Contract/freeze phase only — no runtime behavior changes, no execution capability; no file under `src/pcae/` touched. Freezes Runtime Snapshot (112E) as PCAE's stable canonical read-only interface before Advisory Runtime work (113A). Frozen as the canonical read-only interface for six named consumer classes (humans, CLI — implemented; AI agents, Telegram, REST, dashboard/UI, automation — none implemented). Nine-domain schema frozen, transcribed directly from the real 112E implementation (`runtime`, `registry`, `plugins`, `capabilities`, `health`, `governance`, `state`, `version`, `context`); corrects the phase brief's own suggested "principles or maturity" domain against real evidence — `principles` remains a field inside `runtime`, not a tenth top-level domain. JSON compatibility rules frozen: stable top-level keys, additive-only changes within a schema major version (grounded in 112E's own real precedent of adding `context` without breaking anything), removal/rename requires a major version bump, consumers must ignore unknown keys, no secrets/execution handles/mutable internal references. Deliberate versioning decision: no `snapshot_schema_version` field implemented this phase (would contradict the "no runtime behavior changes" hard boundary every prior pure contract-freeze phase has kept) — the full field contract (name, format, compatibility/deprecation/migration rules, exact bump conditions) is frozen instead for a future implementation phase. Human output compatibility frozen (JSON is the machine contract; default output stays concise; `--verbose` may gain read-only sections without a version bump). Future consumers detailed for Telegram, REST, dashboard, AI agents, audit/reporting, and Advisory Runtime (113A) itself — reading Runtime Snapshot as read-only input, never writing to it. Security rules frozen across ten forbidden categories, cross-checked against real 111B/111C/111D/112E adversarial-test evidence. Added `docs/PCAE_RUNTIME_SNAPSHOT_CONTRACT.md`, `docs/PHASE_112_RUNTIME_SNAPSHOT_CONTRACT_FREEZE.md`. 125 new tests (`tests/test_runtime_snapshot_contract.py`), including a direct cross-check of the frozen schema against the real CLI's current JSON output.

- Phase 112E — Runtime Snapshot & Runtime Inspect Context Integration. Implementation phase — integrates Runtime Context (112C/112D) into the Runtime Inspect subsystem via a new canonical Runtime Snapshot model. Observation-only; no execution capability. Added `src/pcae/core/runtime_snapshot.py`: `RuntimeSnapshot` composes 111B's eight Runtime Introspection objects (unchanged, delegated via their own `get_*()` functions) with a new `context: RuntimeContext | None` field, populated by `build_runtime_context_from_repo()` — a read-only bridge reading `.pcae/session.json`/`tasks/active/` through the same already-governed helpers `pcae session bootstrap` uses (no new I/O capability). Populates Runtime Session, the active Task, and Observation state (always populated per 112B §8's "Observation always available" invariant); Active Phase/Intent/Approval/Broker Decision/Evidence remain explicitly reported as unpopulated, since none has a real governed backing source anywhere in this codebase yet (`COMP-003`/`COMP-007` unimplemented). Refactored `commands/runtime_inspect.py`'s `_build_snapshot(registry)` into a three-line delegation to Runtime Snapshot, kept under its original 111C name/signature for full backward compatibility with every pre-existing call site. `pcae runtime inspect`/`--json`/`--verbose` all continue to work; JSON schema gains exactly one new, additive top-level key (`context`), reconfirmed against 111D's own frozen schema-stability tests (deliberately updated to include it, not loosened). Default human-readable output unchanged; new "Runtime Context (112E):" section appears only under `--verbose`. Five pre-existing 111C/111D tests deliberately updated with explanatory comments (import allowlist, stable-schema key set, JSON-flatness constraint, 111A doc-text cross-check) — none silently loosened beyond what the new key required. 35 new tests (`tests/test_runtime_snapshot.py`); all 101 pre-existing `test_runtime_inspect_cli.py`/`test_runtime_inspect_verification.py` tests still pass. Added `docs/PCAE_RUNTIME_SNAPSHOT.md`, `docs/PHASE_112_RUNTIME_SNAPSHOT_INTEGRATION.md`.

- Phase 112D — Runtime Context Verification & Compatibility. Verification/hardening phase only — no new Runtime Context functionality; `src/pcae/core/runtime_context.py` (112C) unchanged. Verified compatibility across all fourteen 110A–112C lineage phase documents, cross-checking `runtime_context.py`'s constants directly against `runtime_introspection.py` (111B, cross-module) and against 112A/112B's own contract text (not just internal self-consistency). Re-verified structural immutability by attempting mutation on every field of every one of the twelve classes (all fail with `FrozenInstanceError`, including through a fully-composed seven-object chain and against the class-level `OWNERSHIP` object). Confirmed relationship-chain integrity end-to-end (`RuntimeSession → TaskContext → PhaseContext → IntentContext → BrokerDecisionContext → ApprovalContext → EvidenceContext`), ownership and persistence metadata against an independently-transcribed expected table (zero drift from 112B), and composition integrity (`RuntimeContext` carries exactly two fields, no god-object drift). Investigated the `fast_green` baseline's one pre-existing failure fresh rather than re-stating it, under two deliberately observed repository states: idle (`4389/4390`, `test_dry_run_simulation.py::Test89dMatrixReadOnly::test_pytest_dry_run_not_blocked` fails) and mid-implementation with this phase's own active task present (`4390/4390`, the identical test passes) — sharpening 112C's "4389/4390" into "a deterministic function of live `tasks/active/` state, not a fixed count," since the test reads the real repo root via `build_simulation(REPO_ROOT, ...)` rather than a hermetic fixture. Confirmed not a regression and documented why repairing it (in `src/pcae/core/dry_run.py` or the test itself) is out of this phase's scope, including the caveat that a future `4390/4390` result alone does not mean it was fixed. 100 new tests (`tests/test_runtime_context_verification.py`). Added `docs/PHASE_112_RUNTIME_CONTEXT_VERIFICATION.md`.

- Phase 112C — Runtime Context Prototype (Observation-Only). Implementation phase — the first live Runtime Context object model, using the contracts frozen in 112A/112B, preserving every non-executing guarantee established through 112B.1. Added `src/pcae/core/runtime_context.py`, implementing all twelve objects 112A froze as inert, immutable (frozen dataclass) records, importing only `dataclasses`/`typing` (no broker, no registry, no shell, no subprocess, no network). Every identity (`session_id` through `observation_id`, plus the three future placeholders) is required and fail-closed-validated non-empty at construction, enforcing 112B's "Identity is immutable and precedes state" invariant at the one point it can be enforced; `RuntimeContext` has no independent identity (112B §2). Implemented via composition — `RuntimeContext` contains `RuntimeSession`, which contains `TaskContext`/`ObservationContext`; `PhaseContext` contains `IntentContext`; the chain composes through `BrokerDecisionContext` → `ApprovalContext` → `EvidenceContext` — with `TaskContext` referencing its `phase_id` rather than nesting a copy, since Task:Phase cardinality is many-to-one (112B §6/§8.1). Deliberately implements 112B's *resolved* Broker-Decision-before-Approval ordering rather than this phase's own brief's pre-resolution diagram, since objective 1 asked for an implementation exactly matching 112B's frozen contracts — documented explicitly as a deviation, not a silent reversion. Every object carries a `lifecycle_stage` field (112A's six-stage vocabulary); the only implemented transition (`observe_context()`) moves `Created`/`Initialized` to `Observed`, returning a new immutable instance — no `complete()`/`archive()`/`update()` exists on any class. Every class carries class-level `OWNERSHIP` (112B §4) and `PERSISTENCE_BUCKET` (112B §5) metadata, represented but never enforced. Repaired three stale forward-looking guard tests (111R/112A/112B) that asserted `runtime_context.py` must not exist — their intended outcome, not a regression — and fixed one latent glob bug found during the same pass (112B's `*phase-112b*` also matched 112B.1's task contract). 105 new tests (`tests/test_runtime_context.py`). Added `docs/PHASE_112_RUNTIME_CONTEXT_PROTOTYPE.md`.

- Phase 112B.1 — Planning & Bootstrap Consistency Hardening. Governance/planning/bootstrap hygiene phase only — no Runtime Context implementation, runtime execution, or execution capability introduced. Repaired `tasks/TODO.md`, which had presented a stale 90-series roadmap as current work long after the 107–112-series arc superseded it: the former table is now clearly relabeled "Historical: Production v1 Path (90-series, superseded)," and a new "Current Roadmap (112-series)" table lists 112A/112B/112B.1 complete with 112C confirmed as next (112D/112E/113A marked explicit tentative candidates, not a committed queue). Corrected the premise that `pcae session bootstrap` already detected this staleness — direct inspection found it never read `tasks/TODO.md` at all; the prior "stale TODO" observation was a human/agent-level inference, not tool behavior. Hardened `pcae session bootstrap --compact`: it now prints an explicit `Recommended next phase: ...` line (extracted from `PROJECT_STATUS.md`'s own inline sentence, previously computed internally but never surfaced in the compact path) and an explicit `Planning note: ...` line comparing `tasks/TODO.md`'s own "🔜 Next" marker against the current phase, stating plainly which source is authoritative and why the other was ignored when they disagree. Added one new operational rule to `CONTEXT_PACK_OPERATIONAL_RULES` stating the precedence directly. Documented a full source-of-truth precedence order (active task contract > phase prompt > `PROJECT_STATUS.md` > canonical roadmap docs > `tasks/TODO.md` > `tasks/DONE.md` > stale handoff snippets) in new `docs/PHASE_112_PLANNING_BOOTSTRAP_CONSISTENCY_HARDENING.md`. Noted, as an explicit limitation rather than silently repeating it: `docs/ROADMAP.md`'s own "Current State" section is similarly stale (still describes "90 phases," "90B complete") but a full refresh is out of this phase's scope. 18 new tests (`tests/test_bootstrap_todo_consistency.py`).

- Fixed a Phase 112B test false positive: `test_task_contract_excludes_src_pcae` matched the literal substring `src/pcae/` anywhere in the archived task contract, including inside the acceptance-criterion prose ("No file under src/pcae/ touched"), rather than checking only the `## Allowed Files` section it was meant to verify. Narrowed the check to that section so the test verifies the intended governance boundary without a false positive once the task contract is moved to `tasks/done/`.

- Phase 112B — Runtime Context Contract Freeze. Contract/freeze phase only — no Runtime Context implementation, persistence implementation, or execution capability introduced; no file under `src/pcae/` touched. Second phase of the 112-series. Freezes the canonical Runtime Context contracts for every one of 112A's twelve objects before any implementation begins. Adds a new principle, **Identity precedes state**: a Context object's identity must be frozen before its state contract is meaningful, since `Created` (112A) is the act of identity assignment itself, not a step preceding it. Freezes twelve identity contracts (`session_id` through `rollback_id`, plus `RuntimeContext`'s explicit non-identity as a root aggregate), each specifying uniqueness, immutability, lifetime, and ownership, grounded in two real precedents (`task_id`'s `YYYYMMDD-HHMM-<slug>` format, `phase_id`'s bare identifier format) without inventing new ones. Freezes one canonical six-stage state contract (`Created → Initialized → Observed → Updated → Completed → Archived`) shared by all twelve objects, with valid/invalid transitions, a terminal-state rule, and per-object reachable ceilings today. Freezes per-object ownership (creates/owns/updates/archives/observes), extending 112A's category-level split so no Plugin, Broker, or Registry ever creates or owns a Context object. Refines 112A's persistence model into four buckets (Persistent, Session-only, Future persistence, Never persist) for all twelve objects, sharpening 112A's shared "session-only/ephemeral" wording for Broker Decision and Observation state into distinct buckets grounded in 109D's already-frozen "produced and discarded" evidence. Resolves the relationship chain's Approval/Broker-Decision ordering to **Intent → Broker Decision → Approval → Evidence → (future) Execution → (future) Audit → (future) Rollback**, citing 110A §5's frozen "Decision Pipeline → Approval" interface and 110A §8's frozen state sequence. Freezes nine invariants: 112A's seven, with "Phase belongs to one Task" resolved into "at most one Task is active per Phase at any given moment" (reconciling cumulative lifetime cardinality with concurrent-moment cardinality as two different, both-true axes), plus two new invariants — "Broker Decision precedes Approval" and "Identity is immutable and precedes state." Both findings 112A explicitly deferred are resolved here with cited evidence, not assumed by default. Added `docs/PCAE_RUNTIME_CONTEXT_CONTRACT.md`, `docs/PHASE_112_RUNTIME_CONTEXT_CONTRACT_FREEZE.md`. `docs/ROADMAP.md` evaluated, no change needed. 143 new tests (`tests/test_runtime_context_contract.py`), a pure documentation-verification suite. Recommended next phase: 112C — Runtime Context Prototype (Observation-Only).

- Phase 112A — Runtime Context Architecture. Architecture/design phase only — no Runtime Context implementation, persistence implementation, or execution capability introduced; no file under `src/pcae/` touched. First phase of the 112-series. Designs how PCAE models the current operational state of the Runtime while preserving the complete non-executing guarantees established through 111R. Restates the core principle — Runtime orchestrates, Registry resolves, Plugins implement, Metadata precedes behavior, Visibility precedes authority — and extends it with this phase's own addition, **Context precedes execution**: a future execution-capability phase must be able to name the exact session/task/phase/intent/approval/decision an action belongs to before that action could ever be authorized. Defines Runtime Context as the Runtime's dynamic operational model — describes, never executes — generalizing 110C §8's own "Dynamic runtime... a future phase, not implemented here" and completing the design 111B's deferred `SessionInfo`/`TaskInfo`/`PhaseInfo` needed. Freezes the Persistent vs Session Context split (Persistent: Runtime identity, Registry, plugin/capability metadata, version, contracts; Session: Session, Task, Phase, Intent, Approval state, Broker decision, Evidence, Observation state), explicitly clarified as a scope distinction, not a disk-persistence distinction. Freezes twelve context objects, design only: `RuntimeContext`, `RuntimeSession`, `TaskContext`, `PhaseContext`, `IntentContext`, `ApprovalContext`, `BrokerDecisionContext`, `EvidenceContext`, `ObservationContext`, plus three future/stub objects — `ExecutionContext` (current state: `execution_unavailable`), `AuditContext`, `RollbackContext`. Freezes a six-stage Context Lifecycle (`Created → Initialized → Observed → Updated → Completed → Archived`), a third, distinct lifecycle vocabulary alongside 110A §8's Runtime State Model and 110B §4's Plugin Lifecycle, deliberately not a competitor to either. Freezes ownership: Runtime owns Context lifecycle/current context/transitions; Registry owns metadata; Plugins own capability implementation; Broker owns policy decisions; Context never owns execution, approval decisions, or policy evaluation — the third instance, across this arc, of the "surfaces facts, never decides" discipline (110C §5, 111A §1, now this document). Freezes the Context relationship chain (Session → Task → Phase → Intent → Approval → Broker Decision → Evidence → future Execution), recording two evidence-grounded findings rather than assuming an answer: Task:Phase cardinality is many-to-one, verified directly against this session's own operational pattern (every 110–111 series phase was served by one-or-more governed tasks, never the reverse of a single task spanning multiple phases); and an ordering tension between Approval and Broker Decision against 110A §5's frozen "Decision Pipeline → Approval" interface, named explicitly as an open question for 112B rather than silently resolved. Freezes a Persistence Model — the direct, per-concept (not uniform) answer to 111R's recommendation condition: Session/Task/Phase should, and already do, persist; Intent recommended session-only until Evidence exists to make its persistence accountable (fail-closed reasoning); Approval and Evidence should eventually persist once implemented, with nothing to persist yet; Broker decision and Observation state are deliberately session-only/ephemeral as a *continuation* of 109B–109D's already-frozen "consult and discard" safety property, not a new choice — persisting them is declared explicitly out of 112A's scope entirely, requiring its own dedicated future phase with a safety re-analysis. What must never persist (secrets, credentials, tokens, raw untyped manifest content) is inherited unchanged from 111A §8 and 110E/110F/111C's manifest-exclusion precedent. Freezes seven Context invariants, including one named, unresolved tension ("Phase belongs to one Task," contradicting the relationship section's own Task:Phase evidence-grounded finding — left for 112B to resolve deliberately rather than papered over). - Phase 111R — Runtime Architecture Review. Review/documentation phase only — no source behavior changes, no Runtime Context, no execution capability introduced; no file under `src/pcae/` touched. A deliberate architectural checkpoint across the nine phases (110A–111D) that built the PCAE Runtime subsystem, before starting the Runtime Context track. Every finding was produced by a runnable check against live source, live CLI output, or live doc text — direct `dir()` inspection of `RuntimeRegistry`/`runtime_introspection`'s public surface, direct reading of every reviewed module's actual import statements, a live `pcae runtime --help`/`pcae --help` invocation, and a live `PermissionBroker().evaluate()` call — rather than re-summarizing what each prior phase already claimed about itself. Reviews responsibility separation (Runtime, Registry, Plugins, Introspection, Runtime Inspect CLI, Permission Broker, Observation Integration — no creep found in any, verified against live code surface not documentation), dependency direction (full import graph traced and confirmed acyclic; `runtime_registry.py` and `permission_broker_foundation.py` confirmed zero-dependency leaves; broker isolation confirmed), plugin isolation/extensibility (all twelve example future plugins — Claude/Codex/DeepSeek/Telegram/REST/VS Code intent sources, Shell/Git/Filesystem/Backend adapters, Notification providers, Audit/storage providers — confirmed to map onto the ten already-frozen categories with zero code change required to register their metadata), registry and introspection purity (reconfirmed via direct inspection, not re-trust), Runtime Inspect CLI (output usefulness, JSON stability, machine/human readability, safety all reconfirmed; long-term usefulness for AI agents flagged Medium risk since plugin/capability sections are structurally always empty due to no cross-invocation persistence — a direct, correct consequence of 110E's design, not a defect), safety invariants (reconfirmed live including a fresh `PermissionBroker().evaluate()` call; no invariant has weakened at any point across 110A–111D), and Runtime Context (112A) readiness (Session/Task/Phase have real precedents but are not yet introspection-modeled per 111B's deferral; Intent/Approval/Broker-decision/Evidence have no persistence model at all today — flagged as the central open design question 112A must resolve explicitly, not inherit implicitly from the Registry's in-memory-only choice). Seven-item risk register, none Blocker: two Strengths (R-2: the ten-category taxonomy comfortably covers all twelve named future plugin types; R-6: the Registry's implementation pattern — frozen records, passive store, shared validation between admission and re-audit — is a proven, directly reusable template for Runtime Context's new object types) and five Low/Medium risks (R-1: the CLI imports `RuntimeRegistry`/`INTEGRATION_REGISTRY` directly rather than exclusively through Introspection, a minor layering impurity not a reverse dependency; R-3: manifest exclusion from CLI output is a convention living in the CLI layer, not enforced at the Introspection layer itself; R-4: `pcae runtime inspect`'s plugin/capability sections are structurally always empty, limiting practical usefulness for an AI agent asking "what is registered right now"; R-5: Intent/Approval/Broker-decision/Evidence have no persistence model at all, a design question 112A itself must resolve; R-7: roughly thirty unrelated, pre-existing `pcae runtime-*` top-level advisory commands from an earlier, unrelated design-only series share a naming prefix with, but have no relationship to, this arc's `pcae runtime` command group). Recommendation: **Proceed to 112A**, with one condition — 112A's own phase brief should explicitly require a documented Persistence Model decision for each of Intent, Approval, Broker decision, and Evidence, mirroring 110E's own explicit, documented in-memory-only choice for the Registry, not silently inherited or assumed uniform across all four. One hardening fix, within the verification/hardening boundary: `PluginDescriptor.manifest` is now a `MappingProxyType` snapshot taken at construction (`__post_init__` + `object.__setattr__`), closing an aliasing gap where a caller-held manifest dict reference could mutate already-registered metadata even though the dataclass itself is frozen — proven by dedicated tests including one that mutates the original dict after registration and confirms the stored descriptor is unaffected; deliberately a shallow, not deep, copy (documented limitation). - Phase 108C — Permission Broker Policy Composition & Hardening. - Phase 108A — Permission Broker Foundation. Implements the foundational Permission Broker for PCAE as an isolated policy-evaluation subsystem — the first implementation phase after the governance architecture (107A–107E) was frozen. Adds `src/pcae/core/permission_broker_foundation.py`: a stateless `PermissionBroker` class with `evaluate(request) -> decision`, a frozen `PermissionBrokerRequest` model (request_id, timestamp, action_type, execution_class, task_id, phase_id, requested_component, requested_capability, requested_resource, evidence_available, approval_present, simulation_only), and a frozen `PermissionBrokerDecision` model (decision, decision_reason, matched_no_go_ids, matched_invariants, required_remediation, requires_human, simulation_only, implementation_status). Fail-closed: unknown action types, unsupported execution classes, unrecognized components, missing task contracts, and missing evidence all resolve to `DENY`; missing human approval resolves to `HUMAN_REVIEW`; a real (non-simulation) execution attempt always denies because no execution boundary exists. Every decision — including `ALLOW` — carries `implementation_status="execution_unavailable"`; `ALLOW` means only "policy would allow this if execution existed" (`INV-008`), never an executable authorization. The module is fully isolated: no dependency on `shell_gate`, `backend_invocations`, `notifications`, or any other execution-adjacent module — verified by a dedicated AST-based test asserting every import resolves to the Python standard library only. Makes PCAE's validation pipeline fully `pytest-xdist` compatible by eliminating the known parallel-execution artifact collision documented in Phase 107C's Validation Note (11 tests across 4 pre-existing files). Root cause: `tests/test_execution_readiness_preflight_artifact_trust.py`, `tests/test_governed_execution_preflight_artifact_trust.py`, `tests/test_governed_execution_preflight_contract.py`, and `tests/test_execution_readiness_preflight_contract.py` invoked `pcae execution-readiness`/`governed-execution` preflight/show/verify subprocesses (and, via their `clean_artifact_dir` fixtures, in-process save/load calls) against a relative `.pcae/` artifact path resolved against the real, shared repository root rather than an isolated per-test directory, so concurrent xdist workers could race on the same file. Fixed by isolating all 31 affected subprocess invocations to pytest's `tmp_path` fixture and all 4 `clean_artifact_dir` fixtures via `monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path)`. Found and fixed 2 release-critical defects: (1) `pcae health`/`pcae check` crashed with an unhandled `subprocess.CalledProcessError` traceback outside a git repository — added a narrowly-scoped catch in `cli.py::main()` for `git`-prefixed subprocess failures specifically, after an initial attempt using a new custom exception type broke 40 existing tests (e.g. `core/provenance.py::_safe_git_branch`) that already caught the raw exception type; (2) the sdist swept in the entire repository by default (44,399 files, ~6.4MB, including local `.claude/settings.local.json` and `.pcae/session.json`/`provenance-history.json`) while the wheel was already correctly scoped — added `[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist] include = ["src/pcae", "README.md", "LICENSE", "pyproject.toml"]` (sdist now 117 files, ~1.1MB). Verified the golden workflow smoke-tests cleanly against a fresh `git clone` and that Telegram is safely skippable when unconfigured. Added `docs/PHASE_106_PACKAGING_INSTALLATION_CLEAN_SMOKE_TEST.md` and `docs/V0_1_CLEAN_SMOKE_TEST.md`; updated `docs/INSTALLATION.md`, `docs/RELEASE_SCOPE_V0_1.md`, and `docs/V0_1_GOLDEN_WORKFLOW.md`. No packaging blockers remain. 20 new tests (`tests/test_packaging_installation_smoke_v0_1.py`). Non-executing. Recommends 106E — v0.1 Release Candidate.
- Phase 106C — Golden Workflow Stabilization. Added `docs/V0_1_GOLDEN_WORKFLOW.md`: the command-verified v0.1 operator golden workflow, turning `docs/RELEASE_SCOPE_V0_1.md`'s scope into a concrete sequence — start-of-phase (`pcae health/check/doctor task-memory/notify status/phase-report show --latest --trust/phase-report trust --json`), task/phase setup (`pcae task new`), implementation (stay within task-contract scope, no raw commit/push), pre-finalization (`pcae check/phase-report trust --json/push check`), finalization (`pcae skill invoke phase-finalization/commit implementation/task finish --commit/push check/push`), and post-completion verification (`phase-report show --latest --trust/phase-report trust --json/git rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD`). Documents required vs. optional-diagnostic commands and an explicit unsupported-flows list (raw git commit/push, `--no-verify`, force push, shell mediation, Telegram inbound, rollback execution). Every command was verified via `--help`/direct invocation, none invented. Updated `docs/RELEASE_SCOPE_V0_1.md` to reference the golden workflow as a required release artifact. 32 new tests (`tests/test_v0_1_golden_workflow.py`), including lightweight `--help`-only CLI availability checks. Documentation/testing-only; no product code changed. Non-executing. Recommends 106D — Packaging / Installation / Clean-Smoke Test.
- Phase 106B — Release-Critical Warning / Fast-Green Triage. Fixed the 3 fast-green failures carried since before 105A. Root cause 1: `core/backend_invocations.py` defined `VALID_PREFLIGHT_STATUSES` twice at module scope for two unrelated features (94U-era adapter preflight vs. a later execution-readiness-preflight feature) — the later definition silently shadowed the earlier one, so `BackendAdapterPreflightResult.validate()` and `verify_backend_adapter_preflight_artifact()` validated against the wrong status set, always failing with `"unknown preflight status: 'ready'"` (`Test94UPreflightArtifact::test_verify_valid_artifact`, `Test94UPreflightArtifactCLI::test_verify_latest_after_save`). Renamed the 94U constant to `VALID_ADAPTER_PREFLIGHT_STATUSES` and updated its 2 call sites; the unrelated later constant and its own tests are untouched. Root cause 2: `TestBackendShow::test_show_missing_artifacts` ran `pcae backend show --latest` against `cwd=REPO_ROOT` and expected no artifacts to exist — but this long-lived local checkout has 4,760+ real, gitignored `.pcae/backend-invocations/` files accumulated from years of legitimate dogfooding (confirmed empirically: temporarily isolating the directory made the test pass immediately; restored unchanged). Isolated the test to a `tmp_path` cwd instead. **Fast-green is now fully green: 4390/4390** (was 4387/4390). `pcae doctor task-memory` confirmed clean. Added `docs/PHASE_106_RELEASE_CRITICAL_WARNING_FAST_GREEN_TRIAGE.md`; updated `docs/RELEASE_SCOPE_V0_1.md`'s validation baseline and release-blocker table to reflect the resolved disposition. 20 new tests (`tests/test_release_critical_triage_v0_1.py`) plus the 2 repaired tests. Non-executing. Recommends 106C — Golden Workflow Stabilization.

Documentation-only; no code changes. 16 new tests (`tests/test_release_scope_v0_1.py`). Recommends 106B — Release-Critical Warning / Fast-Green Triage.
- Phase 105D — Phase Report Trust Gate Hard-Fail / Push-Check Integration. `pcae phase complete` now hard-fails (exit 1) by default when report trust is incomplete/invalid (95M.1 gate OR 105A/105B+push-state gate), with `--allow-partial-report` as an explicit opt-out that still never dispatches Telegram for a partial report. `pcae push check` gained a `phase_report_trust: passed/failed/skipped` gate validating the latest report's content completeness (missing fields, placeholders) — deliberately excludes push-state fields (`pushed_status`/`origin_main_head`/`pcae_push_check`), since requiring the report to already say "pushed" would make push-check permanently unpassable for the normal pre-push task-finish moment. `pcae task finish --commit` unchanged (warning-only pre-push, per 105C.1). Promoted `apply_push_state_gate`, `PUSH_STATE_FIELDS`, and new `compute_final_trust` to `core/phase_report_trust.py` so `commands/push.py` and `commands/phase.py` share the same logic `commands/task.py` already had; `commands/task.py` keeps its old private names as aliases. Updated 9 `test_phase.py` fixtures and 3 pre-existing 105B/105C/105C.1 tests to reflect the new default (`--allow-partial-report` or updated exit-code expectations). 29 new tests (`tests/test_phase_report_trust_hard_fail.py`). Non-executing. Recommends 106A — v0.1 Release Scope Freeze.
- Phase 105C.1 — Task Finish Report Notification Ordering / Completeness Repair. Repaired a real defect in 105C: `pcae task finish --commit` dispatched Telegram whenever `PCAE_NOTIFY_ENABLED`/sinks were configured, without checking whether final push state (`pushed_status`, `origin_main_head`, `governance_results.pcae_push_check`) was known — 105C's own completion report was sent partial as a result. Added `_apply_push_state_gate()` in `commands/task.py`, folding the OLD (95M.1) schema's push-state-aware missing fields into the 105A/105B trust result used for the dispatch decision (the 105A/105B schema alone treats `pushed_status="not_pushed"` as a valid non-placeholder value, so it never caught this). `_finalize_task_report_and_notify()` now builds a no-I/O trial report to compute this gated trust result before deciding to dispatch: partial/incomplete reports are still finalized (written, visible) but Telegram/any sink is suppressed for that call (`notification_status: "skipped_incomplete"`), and `.pcae/phase-reports/.last-notified.json` is only written on an actual successful send, so a later complete finalization can still send. `pcae phase complete` unchanged. 22 new tests (`tests/test_task_finish_notification_ordering.py`). Non-executing. Recommends 105D.
- Phase 105C — Task Finish Report Trust / Telegram Notification Integration. Integrated `finalize_phase_report()` (phase-completion report build + trust validation + Telegram outbound dispatch) into `pcae task finish --commit`, closing the gap where the real phase-closing workflow never triggered report/notification creation (only `pcae phase complete` did). Added `_finalize_task_report_and_notify()` in `commands/task.py`: reads `.pcae/phase-completion-metadata.json` (skips cleanly with a warning if absent/invalid), builds and trust-validates the report via the same 105A/105B validator `pcae phase complete` uses, and dispatches notifications when `PCAE_NOTIFY_ENABLED`/sinks are configured. Warning-only (hard-fail deferred to 105D). Added a small idempotency marker (`.pcae/phase-reports/.last-notified.json`) to avoid duplicate sends for the same phase_id+commit. `pcae task finish` human/JSON output now reports `Report trust`, `Repair required`, `Report notification`, `Telegram: outbound-only`, `report_path`, `metadata_path`. `pcae phase complete` unchanged. 19 new tests. Non-executing. Recommends 105D — Hard-Fail / Push-Check Integration.

### 89E — Dry-Run Simulation UX Refinement and Operator Guidance (2026-06-28)

Refined human-readable dry-run output with structured sections per decision type:
SIMULATED BLOCK (Type/Override/Governed alternative), SIMULATED DENY (PERMANENT),
SIMULATED REVIEW REQUIRED (GATE distinction, redaction warning), SIMULATED ALLOW
(explicit non-authorization note), SIMULATED REQUIREMENT, and SIMULATED EVIDENCE
REQUIRED. Fixed next-action wording (pcae dry-run explain, not advisory explain).
Enhanced footer as active "PCAE did NOT" checklist. Source changed: _print_human_readable
refactored into 7 focused helper functions. JSON schema, all safety invariants,
and full test suite preserved. Fast-green: 3,221/26.67s. Full suite: 9,311 pass.
Delivers `docs/PHASE_89_DRY_RUN_BLOCKING_SIMULATION_UX_REFINEMENT.md`. Recommends 89F.

### 89A — Advisory Mode Hardening / False-Positive Repair (2026-06-28)

Fixed 3 known false positives and 1 false negative from 88Y. Added known
shells list (bash, sh, zsh, dash, fish, ksh, tcsh, csh) so shell programs
are recognized and require human review rather than blocked as unknown.
Shell -c/-lc flags now extract and classify embedded commands directly,

redacted). env argument inspection differentiates program execution (env python)
from secret variable assignment (env OPENAI_API_KEY=x cmd), fixing the
88V.1 env/printenv over-classification. All 88V.1 secret redaction rules and
hard-block decisions preserved. 1,054 focused tests pass; fast-green unchanged
at ~3,001/~25s. Delivers
`docs/PHASE_89_ADVISORY_MODE_HARDENING_FALSE_POSITIVE_REPAIR.md`. Recommends 89B.

### 88Y.5 — Project State Shared Evidence Optimization (2026-06-27)

Performance optimization. Extended the shared evidence model from 88Y.3/88Y.4
to the five upstream build functions by adding an optional `ctx=None` parameter
to `build_memory_snapshot`, `build_governance_timeline`, `build_decision_log`,
`build_risk_register`, and `build_project_state`. Updated `GateDryRunContext`
property methods to pass `ctx=self`, so each build function is called exactly
once per gate dry-run invocation instead of repeatedly through the cascade.
Key finding: `build_governance_timeline`, `build_decision_log`, and
`build_risk_register` each called their upstream build functions but never used
the returned values — these vestigial calls are skipped entirely when ctx is
provided. Also eliminates 4 redundant git subprocess calls inside
`build_project_state` by deriving git data from ctx properties. Per-call runtime
reduced from 9.16s to 3.22s (-65%); cumulative reduction from original 88Y.2
baseline: 20.86s → 3.22s (-85%). Added 24 tests in `test_project_state_context.py`
covering decision equivalence (8), memoization (7), freshness (2),
no-persistence (2), backward compatibility (4), idempotency (1). Fixed one test
in `test_gate_dry_run_context.py` tracking function to accept `ctx` kwarg.
No gate decisions, output schema, or governance rules changed. No persistent
cache, no global cache, no cross-invocation cache. Doc at
`docs/PHASE_88_PROJECT_STATE_SHARED_EVIDENCE_OPTIMIZATION.md`. Next: 88Z.

### 88Y.4 — Gate Dry-Run Decision Equivalence and Performance Matrix (2026-06-27)

Validation and hardening phase. Fixed None-sentinel memoization bug in
`GateDryRunContext` — properties returning `None` (task_contract, git_porcelain,
git_branch, git_ahead_count) were recomputed on every access because `None`
doubled as the "not yet computed" sentinel. Introduced `_UNSET = object()`
sentinel. Expanded `test_gate_dry_run_context.py` from 20 to 55 tests
covering 14 representative scenarios (idle, source mutation, forbidden
mutation, policy-forbidden, backend known/unknown, adoption, commit, push,
all-flags). Decision-equivalence invariants verified across all scenarios:
gate count=15, names/order preserved, hard blocks denied, authorization/
enforcement always false, audit evidence shape lists, no redaction applied.
Memoization verified: _detect_task_contract 15→1 call, git evidence ≤3
calls per invocation. Freshness confirmed across separate invocations.
No persistent cache, no global cache, no module-level mutable state.
No tests deleted/skipped/xfailed. No assertions weakened. No production
behavior changed beyond sentinel fix. Doc at docs/PHASE_88_GATE_DRY_RUN_
DECISION_EQUIVALENCE_AND_PERFORMANCE_MATRIX.md. Next: 88Z.

### 88V.1 — Secret Redaction and Deny Mapping Repair (2026-06-27)

Enforcement-readiness repair phase. Fixes four gaps documented in 88U/88V:

- **GAP-1 VAR=val secret redaction**: Secret-like VAR=val command prefixes
  (OPENAI_API_KEY, TOKEN, PASSWORD, etc.) now detected as secret_access with
  full command redaction in broker output.
- **GAP-2 env/printenv secret exposure**: `env` and `printenv` removed from
  read-only programs; now classified as secret_access.
- **GAP-3 broker.requested_command redaction**: `broker.requested_command`
  now redacted when secret_access detected; serialized JSON output is safe.
- **GAP-4 deny mapping**: Shell-gate `deny` now maps to `blocked_by_shell_gate`
  (a hard block decision), closing enforcement boundary gap.

`_is_secret_env_var_name`, `_SECRET_VAR_NAME_SUBSTRINGS`, env/printenv handler,
fixed path stripping for VAR=val), `src/pcae/core/permission_broker.py`
(requested_command redaction, deny mapping fix). 43 new fast-green tests
(2,709 total). No enforcement, shell interception, or backend invocation.

- Broker + Shell Gate Integration Design (Phase 88S): design-only phase producing `docs/PHASE_88_BROKER_SHELL_GATE_INTEGRATION_DESIGN.md` (version 0.1, status draft_documented, implementation_status not_started). Defines how the permission broker prototype should consume and interpret shell-gate evidence in a future 88T integration prototype. Covers: (1) Evidence fields — 21 shell-gate fields the broker must consume, fields to reject (performed/authorization flags if true), and command text redaction policy (SHA-256 hash when secret_access_detected; no raw text in audit records); (2) Full decision mapping — all 26 SGP_DECISIONS → 24 BPE_DECISIONS with priority column and hard-block flag; key changes from 88R: `blocked_by_missing_task` → `blocked_by_task_contract` promoted to priority 1 hard block (was falling through to missing evidence), `blocked_by_policy_forbidden_file` → `blocked_by_scope` for audit consistency with scope preflight, `requires_active_task` + no task → `blocked_by_task_contract` hard block; (3) Category mapping — all 24 SGP_CATEGORIES with broker implications and hard-block column; (4) 12-level integrated decision priority chain for 88T `_broker_decide`: SG hard blocks (1a force push, 1b raw git push, 1c SG hard block map, 1d requires_active_task+no_task) → malformed/contradictory evidence → evidence failures → test run lock → no active task → scope denial → missing evidence → human review → allow_preflight_only; (5) Hard-block propagation rules for force push, raw git push, destructive filesystem, policy-forbidden file, test run lock, and unknown — all unconditional, no human approval or accepted risk override; (6) Non-hard-block handling: `requires_human_review` satisfied by human_review_present; `requires_preflight` → missing evidence + scope check; `requires_active_task` when task present → no block; `requires_more_evidence` → missing evidence; all SG allow decisions → allow_preflight_only maximum; (7) Human approval limits — satisfies human-review gate only; never overrides hard blocks; does not grant execution authorization; (8) Accepted risk limits — recorded in evidence; never overrides hard blocks; never satisfies human review gate; (9) Missing SG evidence — requires_more_evidence (never allow); (10) Contradiction detection — 7 specific contradictions all → `blocked_by_conflicting_evidence` hard block; (11) Performed-flag invariant — all 14 flags unconditionally false, invariant survives hard blocks, human approval, accepted risk; (12) Audit model — 11 new fields for 88T: shell_gate_schema_version, shell_gate_command_category, shell_gate_command_text_hash, shell_gate_command_text_redacted, shell_gate_decision, shell_gate_reason_codes, shell_gate_hard_block_present, conflicting_evidence_detected, conflicting_evidence_details, hard_block_sources, human_review_sources, accepted_risk_noted, broker_mapping_reason; (13) Security requirements — schema version validation (block if missing or wrong), malformed evidence type checking (unknown category or allow decision + hard_block=True → contradiction), conservative handling (block when uncertain), no trust amplification (SG allow ≠ execution authorization); (14) Minimum 102-test suite specification for 88T (hard-block propagation 8+, non-hard-block 6+, read-only 3+, malformed evidence 5+, performed-flag invariant 56 parametrized, secret redaction 2+, contradiction 4+, active-task boundary 4+); (15) Recommended implementation sequence: 88T prototype → 88U validation → 88V schema hardening; (16) 20 safety invariants. Decision priority chain (8 levels): (1) shell gate hard blocks — force push > raw git push > raw git commit > history rewrite > destructive filesystem > policy forbidden > other; (2) explicit evidence failures — health > check > doctor > tests > push check; (3) test run lock (when expensive test execution detected); (4) no active task for mutating actions; (5) scope preflight denial; (6) missing evidence → `requires_more_evidence`; (7) human review gate → `requires_human_review`; (8) all clear → `allow_preflight_only`. 24 broker decision values in `BPE_DECISIONS`.
