- Shell Gate Test Matrix and False-Positive Review (Phase 88Q): hardens the Phase 88P shell gate classifier by adding compound command parsing, pipe/tee write detection, backend/secret/environment classification, and a comprehensive command-category test matrix. Classifier changes to `src/pcae/core/shell_gate.py`: (1) compound command parsing — `&&`, `||`, `;` operators split token list into segments; most-restrictive category (by `_CATEGORY_SEVERITY` ordering) wins; reason code `compound_command_detected` prepended; (2) pipe/tee write detection — `cmd | tee <path>` detects tee target, classifies write category (`policy_forbidden_file_mutation` / `source_mutation` / `test_mutation` / `docs_mutation` / `filesystem_write`); pure pipe chains use most-restrictive segment; (3) `_BACKEND_PROGRAMS` frozenset — `claude`, `claude-deepseek`, `codex`, `openai`, `anthropic`, `gemini`, `vertex` → `backend_invocation` (previously `unknown`); (4) `_SECRET_ACCESS_PROGRAMS` frozenset — `security`, `pass`, `gpg`, `op`, `vault`, etc. → `secret_access`; (5) `_SECRET_FILE_PREFIXES` — `cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa`, `cat ~/.aws/credentials`, `cat ~/.kube/config`, etc. → `secret_access` (previously `read_only_inspection` FALSE NEGATIVE); (6) environment mutation: `export VAR=val`/`unset VAR` → `environment_mutation`, `source file`/`. file` → `environment_mutation`, `VAR=val cmd` env-var prefix → `environment_mutation`; (7) filesystem permission changes: `chmod`, `chown`, `chgrp`, `chattr`, `ln` → `filesystem_write` (previously `unknown`); (8) `python -m pip install` → `package_install` (previously `unknown`). Internal refactor: `_classify_command` renamed to `_classify_single`; new `_classify_command` wrapper handles compound/pipe routing; new helpers: `_empty_flags`, `_split_on_operators`, `_find_tee_write_target`, `_most_restrictive_classification`, `_is_secret_file_access`. False negatives fixed: `echo x | tee README.md` → `policy_forbidden_file_mutation`; `cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa` → `secret_access`; `git status && rm -rf /` → `destructive_filesystem`; `pcae health && git push` → `raw_git_push`. All 155 existing `tests/test_shell_gate.py` tests preserved unchanged. New `tests/test_shell_gate_matrix.py`: 287 tests across 24 test classes (category matrix, idle/active, compound, pipe/tee, redirection, backend/secret/environment, performed-flag invariant, boundary, false-positive review, false-negative review, helper unit tests). `tests/conftest.py` updated: `test_shell_gate_matrix` added to `FAST_GREEN_MODULES`. Creates `docs/PHASE_88_SHELL_GATE_TEST_MATRIX.md`. Classifier-only boundary preserved: no execution, no shell interception, no shell wrappers, no backend invocation, no permission broker, all performed flags unconditionally false. Fast-green: 2,234 passed / 22.66s (was 1,947). Quick tier: 7,508 passed / 2:08 (was 7,221). Full suite: 8,220 passed / 0:27:24, 0 failures (was 7,933). Recommends 88R — Permission Broker Prototype.

- Shell Gate Prototype (Phase 88P): implements the first shell gate classifier as a read-only command analysis command `pcae shell-gate check --command "<cmd>" [--json]`. Classifies proposed shell commands into 23 categories (88O taxonomy) and returns one of 26 decision values with a structured JSON envelope. Never executes the command text. New source: `src/pcae/core/shell_gate.py` (classifier + `build_shell_gate`), `src/pcae/commands/shell_gate.py` (CLI runner), CLI registration in `src/pcae/cli.py`. Classification: read-only programs (ls, pwd, cat, grep, find, sed -n, awk) → `allow_read_only`; git read-only subcommands → `allow_read_only`; `git push` → `blocked_by_raw_git_push`; `git push --force/-f/--force-with-lease` → `blocked_by_force_push`; `git commit` → `blocked_by_raw_git_commit`; `git rebase/reset --hard/cherry-pick` → `blocked_by_history_rewrite`; `rm -rf`/`git clean -fd` → `blocked_by_destructive_filesystem`; output redirection `>` to README.md/REAL_CAPTURED_TASKS.md/LINKEDIN_ARTICLE_DRAFT.md → `blocked_by_policy_forbidden_file`; redirection to `src/**` → `source_mutation`; `tests/**` → `test_mutation`; `docs/**` → `docs_mutation`; `pip/brew/npm/cargo install` → `requires_human_review`; `curl/wget/ssh/aws/gh` → `requires_human_review`; `python -m pytest -n auto` → `allow_test_execution` (with test-run preflight check) or `blocked_by_test_run_lock`; `pcae commit/push` → `allow_governed`; all other pcae subcommands → `allow_governed`; unrecognized program → `blocked_by_unknown_command`. All performed flags unconditionally false (`authorization_granted`, `execution_authorized`, `command_executed`, `repo_mutation_performed`, `backend_invocation_performed`, `prompt_sent`, `capture_performed`, `intake_performed`, `adoption_performed`, `raw_git_push_performed`, `force_push_performed`, `storage_written`). Policy-forbidden files checked via `_SGP_POLICY_FORBIDDEN_FILES` tuple (identical to `_SPF_POLICY_FORBIDDEN_FILES`). Expensive pytest (`-n` flag) calls `pcae doctor test-run --json` read-only to check `clear_to_run`. Adds `tests/test_shell_gate.py` with 155 fast unit tests (all fast-green tier) across 11 test classes: envelope invariants (10), performed flags always false (80 parametrized), read-only commands (12), raw git commit blocked (4), raw git push blocked (4), force push blocked (5), history rewrite blocked (3), destructive filesystem blocked (4), file write/redirection (5), policy-forbidden file (5), test execution (6), package/network review (5), unknown command (4), pcae governed (4), safety notes (5). Fast-green: 1,947 passed / 22.60s (was 1,792 — 155 new tests added). Quick tier: 7,221 passed / 2:11 (was 7,066). Full suite: 7,933 passed, 0 failed / 28:45. Known limitations: compound commands (`&&`/`;`) only examine first token; shell variable expansion not evaluated; `tee` pipe chain writes not detected; categories backend_invocation/prompt_send/capture/intake/adoption/environment_mutation/secret_access have no program lists yet (conservative: classified as unknown → blocked). Recommends 88Q — Shell Gate Test Matrix and False-Positive Review.
- Scope Matching Shared Utility Reconciliation (Phase 88O.1): eliminates the scope file-pattern matching divergence between `gate_dry_run.py::_evaluate_scope` (which used inline logic: `fnmatch.fnmatch(rf, pat) or rf == pat or rf.startswith(pat.rstrip("*"))`) and `scope_preflight.py::_match_file` (the canonical function already used by `mutation_preflight` and `backend_preflight`). The divergence was: `gate_dry_run` lacked the `if stripped and ...` empty-string guard around its `startswith` check, meaning pattern `"*"` → `stripped=""` → `rf.startswith("")` = always True without the fnmatch guard; `_match_file` would skip that branch since `fnmatch.fnmatch(rf, "*")` already returns True. Fix: in `gate_dry_run.py::_evaluate_scope`, extend the existing late import (`_SPF_POLICY_FORBIDDEN_FILES`) to also import `_match_file`, remove the local `import fnmatch`, and replace the two inline `any()` matching loops with `_match_file(rf, forbidden_patterns)` / `_match_file(rf, list(allowed_patterns))`. No new shared module created; late-import approach maintains the existing circular-import workaround. No other source files changed. Adds `tests/test_scope_matching_consistency.py` with 42 tests: 12 `_match_file` unit tests (exact/glob double-star/single-star/prefix/wildcard/empty), 8 `_SPF_POLICY_FORBIDDEN_FILES` constant tests, 12 Python-level cross-caller consistency tests (all four callers agree on forbidden/allowed classification with mock task contract), 4 no-active-task non-authorising tests (blocked_by_missing/unknown/None/scope_not_evaluated), 5 subprocess CLI consistency tests (scope preflight + gate dry-run + mutation preflight + backend preflight all block README.md; cross-CLI agreement test). Documents prefix-fallback behavior: `_match_file("README.md.bak", ["README.md"])` = True because `startswith("README.md")` — current documented behavior, not changed. Adds `docs/PHASE_88_SCOPE_MATCHING_SHARED_UTILITY_RECONCILIATION.md`. Pre-edit targeted baseline: 168 passed. Post-edit: all 168 tests pass unchanged (22 scope_gate, 63 scope_preflight_review, 47 backend_preflight_review, 36 mutation_preflight_review). Fast-green: 1,792 passed / 31.40s. Quick tier: 7,066 passed / 2:37. Full suite: green (see PROJECT_STATUS.md). Recommends 88P — Shell Gate Prototype.
- Shell Gate Design Reconciliation (Phase 88O): reconciles the Phase 87 shell gate architecture with the concrete Phase 88/88N preflight layer, permission broker reconciliation, fast-green validation architecture, and policy-forbidden consistency work. Delivers `docs/PHASE_88_SHELL_GATE_RECONCILIATION.md` — design-only artifact (version 0.1, draft_documented, implementation_status=not_started). Defines: shell gate role (future mediation layer that observes proposed commands, classifies risk, requires preflight evidence, blocks raw push/force push/policy-forbidden mutations, never executes itself); shell gate non-role (not an executor, not the permission broker, not a replacement for preflights/task-contracts/human-review/pcae health/check/doctor); relationship to permission broker (broker decides policy in principle, gate controls shell execution in practice — both needed, neither replaces the other); relationship to all five explicit preflights (scope/backend/mutation/commit/push outputs are evidence inputs, not authorization); relationship to task contracts (gate enforces but does not define; policy-forbidden files are hard blocks independent of task contract content); no-active-task conservative policy (read-only inspection allowed, all mutating/invocation/test categories require active task or are blocked); command classification taxonomy (23 categories: read_only_inspection, test_execution, pcae_governed_lifecycle, pcae_governed_commit, pcae_governed_push, raw_git_commit, raw_git_push, force_push, git_history_rewrite, destructive_filesystem, filesystem_write, source_mutation, test_mutation, docs_mutation, policy_forbidden_file_mutation, backend_invocation, prompt_send, output_capture, intake_adoption, package_install, network_access, secret_access, environment_mutation, unknown); decision model (26 values: allow_read_only through unknown; unknown always treated as deny); raw git commit policy (blocked when pcae governed path available); raw git push / force push (unconditional hard blocks, no human override at gate level); destructive filesystem policy (default deny, narrow authorization path); shell redirection classified as filesystem_write; package install always requires_human_review; backend/network/API commands require preflight + active task + human review; prompt/capture/intake/adoption gated by full governance chain; test execution policy with test-run preflight requirement (clear_to_run=true before full-suite); tier-aware validation (targeted + fast-green for low/medium risk; quick for pre-push confidence; full for shared governance source changes); fast-green integration (gate must not downgrade or collapse tier model); policy-forbidden file hard blocks independent of task contract; human approval and accepted-risk limits (evidence not bypass; force push blocked even with human approval; accepted risk ≠ mitigation); audit and evidence model (decision_id, reason_codes, command_class, risk_class, evidence_artifacts, 8 audit event types); known gate_dry_run.py scope matching divergence from scope_preflight.py::_match_file (inline fallbacks rf==pat and rf.startswith vs pure fnmatch; documented as risk for future shell gate; corrective phase 88O.1 recommended); future roadmap 88O.1 (scope match shared utility) → 88P (shell gate prototype) → 88Q (test matrix) → 88R (broker prototype) → 88S (broker+gate integration); 17 safety invariants. Design only: no source changes, no test changes, no shell gate implementation, no permission broker implementation, no backend invocation, no shell interception, no storage. - Full Suite Bottleneck Elimination (Phase 88N.4): profiles and eliminates the dominant full-suite runtime bottleneck (28:13 / 1,693s on M5 Pro). Root cause: 115 tests across `test_project_state.py`, `test_risk_register.py`, `test_decision_log.py`, and `test_governance_timeline.py` each called `_run_<command>_json()` independently per test, spawning a fresh Python subprocess per assertion (7–30s each). These files cover PCAE governance commands (project-state, risk-register, decision-log, governance-timeline) whose output never changes between test calls in the same run. Fix: replaced per-test subprocess calls with `@pytest.fixture(scope="module")` fixtures that run each command once per xdist worker and cache the result for all field-checking tests in the module. Determinism tests (e.g., `test_risk_register_risks_are_deterministic`) share two module-scoped runs via `_<name>_data2()` fixture instead of 2 subprocess calls per test (previously 6 subprocess calls total for 3 determinism tests, now 2 per worker). No-mutation behavioral tests (`test_*_no_repository_files_created`, `test_*_no_cache_files_created`) retain own subprocess calls since they require pre/post state comparison. Cross-command smoke tests (`test_*_still_works`) retain own calls since they test distinct commands. Adds `docs/PHASE_88_FULL_SUITE_BOTTLENECK_ELIMINATION.md`. - Task Finish Tracked-File Robustness (Phase 88N.1): fixes `pcae task finish --staged-file-aware --commit` so it succeeds when the active task contract file in `tasks/active/` was never tracked by git. Root cause: `run_task_finish` built `paths_to_stage` unconditionally starting with the old active path; after `finish_active_task` moved the file to `tasks/done/`, `git add -- tasks/active/...md` failed with "pathspec did not match any files" because git had no tracked record of that path. Fix: call `git ls-files --error-unmatch` on the active path before the move; include the old active path in `paths_to_stage` only when `returncode == 0` (tracked). Untracked case: `paths_to_stage` starts empty; `result.updated_files` and `result.completed_task.destination_path` provide the new done path, `tasks/DONE.md`, and session file — which are staged cleanly. Tracked case: behavior identical to before. Skips the pre-existing changes blocker that normally blocks `--commit`. Reports `protected_staged_files_preserved`, `protected_staged_file_hashes_before/after` in JSON. Never pushes, invokes backend, or executes runner. 9 new tests.
- Staged-File-Aware Implementation Commit Mode (Phase 79A): adds `pcae commit implementation --message <msg> --path <path> [--path <path> ...] [--dry-run] [--json]`. - Runner No-Op Trace Review Artifact (Phase 73D): adds `pcae phase runner-execution-trace-review`, `--json`, and `--save` for reviewing runner no-op execution traces. Reports `trace_present`, `noop`, `would_execute`, `mutation_performed`, `review_status` (missing_trace/blocked/ready_for_approval), and `review_reasons`. `--save` persists to `.pcae/runner-execution-trace-reviews/latest.json`. Always `execution_authorized=false`. 4 new tests.
- Shared Multi-Phase Implementation Commit Audit Handling (Phase 73C.1): improves `pcae phase audit` to detect and classify shared multi-phase implementation commits (e.g. "Implement Phases 73A-73C ..."). Shared implementation commits are now reported with `implementation_commit_shared=true`, `shared_commit_phase_ids`, and an advisory warning explaining the shared commit and recommending one-commit-per-phase discipline. Properly paired phases with dedicated implementation commits remain warning-free. Truly missing implementation commits still produce the original missing-implementation warning. 7 new tests.
- Runner No-Op Execution Abort Scenarios (Phase 73C): adds `--scenario` flag to `pcae phase runner-execute --noop` for simulated abort case reporting. Supports 6 scenarios: `dirty-tree`, `active-task`, `denied-request`, `revoked-request`, `queue-empty`, and `authorization-unavailable`. Each reports `abort=true`, `policy_category`, `simulated_condition`, and `suggested_action`. No repository/queue/task/request mutation. `--scenario` requires `--noop`. 6 new tests.
- Runner No-Op Execution Approval Binding (Phase 73B): enhances `pcae phase runner-execute --noop` trace to include governance binding status. Reports `queue_approval_present`, `queue_approval_matches_current_queue`, `simulation_approval_present`, `execution_request_present/denied/revoked`, `authorization_summary_status`, `preflight_status`, `binding_complete`, and `binding_reasons`. Binding complete requires valid non-empty queue, matching queue approval, present non-denied/revoked request. Execution remains unauthorized. 3 new tests.
- Runner No-Op Execution Trace (Phase 73A): adds `--noop`, `--save`, and `--json` to `pcae phase runner-execute`. Produces a structured no-op execution trace with `noop=true`, snapshots of queue validation, queue approval, preflight, authorization summary, runner policy, governance binding status, and refusal reason. `--save` persists to `.pcae/runner-execution-traces/latest.json`. Always `execution_available=false`, `execution_authorized=false`, `would_execute=false`, `mutation_performed=false`. Original refusal behavior preserved without `--noop`. 4 new tests.
- Authorization Lifecycle Summary Artifact (Phase 72Z): adds `pcae phase runner-authorization-summary`, `--json`, and `--save` for a read-only summary of the complete authorization lifecycle. Reports `overall_status` (blocked/incomplete/not_authorized), queue validation, queue approval, simulation approval, execution request lifecycle, request review, denial, and execution authorization gate status. Always `execution_available=false`, `execution_authorized=false`. `--save` persists to `.pcae/runner-authorization-summaries/latest.json`. Missing artifacts handled gracefully. 6 new tests.
- Denied Request Authorization Block (Phase 72Y): enhances `pcae phase runner-execution-authorize` to inspect execution request lifecycle state. JSON output now includes `request_present`, `request_denied`, `request_revoked`, and `authorization_blocked_by_request_state`. Refusal reason explicitly mentions denied/revoked requests or missing request. Command always refuses. 4 new tests.
- Execution Request Preflight Integration (Phase 72X): extends `pcae phase runner-execution-preflight` to include execution request lifecycle status. Adds 4 new requirements: execution request present, execution request not denied, execution request not revoked, and execution request review present. Preflight now reports `execution_request_present`, `execution_request_status` (missing/present/denied/revoked), `execution_request_review_present`, `execution_request_review_status`, `execution_request_denied`, `execution_request_revoked`, and `request_blocks_authorization`. Denied/revoked requests set `request_blocks_authorization=true`. Deny/revoke commands now update the request artifact to reflect lifecycle state. Execution remains unavailable and unauthorized. 5 new tests.
- Execution Authorization Request Denial and Revocation (Phase 72W): adds `pcae phase runner-execution-request-deny`, `--message`, `--json` and `pcae phase runner-execution-request-revoke`, `--message`, `--json` for safely denying and revoking execution authorization requests. Both require an existing request artifact. Denial persists `denied=true`, `execution_authorized=false` to `.pcae/runner-execution-request-denials/latest.json`. Revocation persists `revoked=true`, `execution_authorized=false` to `.pcae/runner-execution-request-revocations/latest.json`. Idempotent: already-denied/revoked requests report the existing state. No queue/task mutation. 6 new tests.
- Execution Authorization Request Review (Phase 72V): adds `pcae phase runner-execution-request-review`, `--json`, and `--save` for evaluating an execution authorization request without approving execution. Reports `review_status` (`missing_request`, `blocked`, `ready_for_denial_or_future_authorization`), `missing_prerequisites`, `approval_granted=false`, `execution_authorized=false`. `--save` persists to `.pcae/runner-execution-request-reviews/latest.json`. 4 new tests.
- Execution Authorization Request Artifact (Phase 72U): adds `pcae phase runner-execution-request`, `--message`, `--dry-run`, `--json` and `pcae phase runner-execution-request-show --json` for creating a non-authorizing execution request. Request records `requested=true`, `approved=false`, `denied=false`, `revoked=false`, `execution_authorized=false`, a governance snapshot (queue validation, simulation presence), and `request_ready`. `--dry-run` reports without writing. Persists to `.pcae/runner-execution-requests/latest.json`. No queue/task mutation. 6 new tests.
- Runner Execution Command Stub Refusal (Phase 72T): adds `pcae phase runner-execute`, `--dry-run`, and `--json` as an explicit stub that always refuses execution. Reports `execution_available=false`, `execution_authorized=false`, `mutation_performed=false`, `tasks_created=0`, `queue_mutated=false` with a clear refusal reason and suggested next steps. Human output unmistakably states execution is not implemented and not authorized. 6 new tests.
- Execution Authorization Artifact Schema Dry Run (Phase 72S): adds `pcae phase runner-execution-authorization-schema` and `--json` for a read-only schema preview of the proposed future execution authorization artifact. Outputs `schema_only=true`, `artifact_written=false`, `execution_authorized=false`, `authorization_available=false`, proposed fields with descriptors, minimum requirements, and forbidden implied-authorization rules. No artifact is written. No queue/task mutation. 5 new tests.
- Execution Authorization Design Record (Phase 72R): adds a formal design record to `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` defining what execution authorization means and what it must not mean. Distinguishes queue approval, simulation approval, runner preflight, and execution authorization as separate decisions. Defines 14 minimum future requirements and 6 forbidden implied-authorization cases. Includes proposed future artifact schema without implementing writing. States current execution authorization remains unavailable. Documentation only; no code behavior changes.
- Queue Preflight Positive Non-Execution Path (Phase 72Q): adds 6 tests proving the positive non-execution path through runner preflight. With a valid fixture queue and matching approval, preflight correctly reports all queue-related requirements met (queue non-empty, queue validation present, queue valid, queue approval present, queue approval matches, queue approval execution_authorized=false) while execution remains `execution_available=false`, `execution_authorized=false`, and `preflight_status=design_only`. Human output clearly states no execution. Tests cover cleared queue revert and fixture cleanup.
- Queue Approval Matching Harden (Phase 72P): adds `pcae phase queue approval-check` and `--json` for a focused readiness check of queue approval state. Checks queue presence, queue validity, approval presence, approval digest match against current queue, and `execution_authorized=false`. Returns exit code 0 only when all checks pass. Tests prove match, mismatch after queue change, empty queue refusal, and execution_authorized=false using fixture queues. 6 new tests.
- Safe Queue Fixture Lifecycle (Phase 72O): adds `pcae phase queue fixture-add`, `--count N`, `--json` and `pcae phase queue fixture-clear`, `--json` for creating and safely removing non-executable test fixture entries. Fixtures are explicitly marked `source_type=fixture`, `fixture=true`, `execution_authorized=false` with deterministic titles (QUEUE-FIXTURE-001, -002, -003). Default count is 1, max is 3. `fixture-clear` removes only fixture entries, preserving all non-fixture entries. Queue validation now reports `fixture_count` and recognizes fixtures as valid. Validation only flags `execution_authorized=true` as forbidden (not `false`). 8 new tests.
- Queue-to-Runner Preflight Bridge (Phase 72N): extends `pcae phase runner-execution-preflight` to include real queue validation and queue approval status. Adds 5 new requirements: queue validation present, queue valid, queue approval present, queue approval matches current queue, and queue approval execution_authorized=false. Preflight output now includes `queue_validation_status`, `queue_valid`, `queue_approval_present`, `queue_approval_matches_current_queue`, and `queue_approval_execution_authorized`. Empty queue, invalid queue, and approval mismatch are detected and reported as unmet requirements. Execution remains `execution_available=false` and `execution_authorized=false`. Total requirements increased from 17 to 22. 7 new tests.
- Queue Approval Artifact (Phase 72M): adds `pcae phase queue approve`, `--json`, `--message`, and `--dry-run` for approving the current phase queue snapshot for future runner consideration. Requires queue validation to pass and queue to be non-empty. Refuses empty or invalid queues. Approval records `approved=true`, `approved_at`, `queue_digest` (SHA-256), `queue_entry_count`, `approval_message`, `approver_source=local_cli`, and `execution_authorized=false`. `--dry-run` reports proposed approval without writing. `pcae phase queue approval-show` and `--json` display the persisted approval including current queue digest match detection. Persists to `.pcae/phase-queue-approvals/latest.json`. No queue mutation, no task creation, no execution. 10 new tests.
- Real Queue Item Validation (Phase 72L): adds `pcae phase queue validate` and `--json` for read-only validation of real phase queue entries. Validates queue readability, entry titles, supported source_type, source_prompt_path for captured_prompt entries, placeholder/dummy detection, duplicate title detection, invalid phase_id patterns, and forbidden execution-authorizing fields. Empty queue is valid but reports `queue_ready=false`. No queue mutation, no task creation, no execution. 15 new tests.
- Execution Authorization Negative Gate (Phase 72K): adds `pcae phase runner-execution-authorize`, `--json`, and `--dry-run` as an explicit negative gate that always refuses execution authorization. Reports `authorization_available=false`, `authorized=false`, `mutation_performed=false`. Tests prove no approval/simulation/preflight path can produce `execution_authorized=true`. Human authority is noted. 5 new tests.
- Runner Simulation Approval Persistence Check (Phase 72J): adds `pcae phase runner-sim-approval-show` and `--json` for inspecting the latest persisted simulation approval artifact. Reports approval presence, approved status, simulation reference, message, approver, and `execution_authorized=false`. Preflight correctly recognizes persisted approval as present/matching, and detects mismatches when simulation is updated after approval. 5 new tests.
- Compact Historical Continuity Summary (Phase 72I): compact bootstrap now summarizes historical strategic continuity in a single line showing decision ID, activation phase, decision basis, and first sentence of the rationale, followed by a "Full details:" pointer. Previously the full multi-paragraph rationale and deferred/referenced blocks were printed even when the decision was historical. Current (non-historical) strategic decisions continue to show full details. 4 new tests.
- Runner Execution Preflight Design (Phase 72H): adds `pcae phase runner-execution-preflight` and `--json` for a design-only preflight specification. Defines 17 requirements for future runner execution including clean tree, health, check, task memory, queue, readiness, plan, policy, simulation, review, approval, and execution authorization. Always reports `preflight_status=design_only`, `execution_available=false`, `execution_authorized=false`. Human authority explicitly stated. 4 new tests.
- Runner Simulation Approval Gate (Phase 72G): adds `pcae phase runner-sim-approve`, `--json`, `--message`, and `--dry-run` for recording human approval of a runner simulation. Requires a review artifact with `ready_for_approval` status. Approval explicitly records `execution_authorized=false`. Refuses if review is missing or blocked. `--dry-run` reports proposed approval without writing. Persists to `.pcae/runner-simulation-approvals/latest.json`. 5 new tests.
- Runner Simulation Review Artifact (Phase 72F): adds `pcae phase runner-sim-review`, `--json`, and `--save` for reviewing the latest runner simulation artifact. Reports `review_status` as `ready_for_approval`, `blocked`, or `missing_simulation`. Includes simulation metadata, readiness summary, and policy summary. `--save` persists to `.pcae/runner-simulation-reviews/latest.json`. Does not approve or execute. 4 new tests.
- Runner Simulation Failure Cases (Phase 72E): extends `pcae phase runner-simulate` with `--scenario` for failure case simulation using the 72B policy matrix. Supports 5 scenarios: `dirty-tree` (hard stop), `active-task` (hard stop), `git-lock` (recoverable stop, suggests `pcae doctor git-lock`), `audit-warning` (advisory warning), and `queue-empty` (continue allowed). JSON output includes `scenario`, `policy_category`, `runner_would_continue`, and `suggested_action`. No repository state is mutated. 8 new tests.
- Runner Simulation Trace Artifact (Phase 72D): adds `pcae phase runner-simulate`, `--json`, `--save`, and `--count N` for dry-run simulation traces. Combines readiness snapshot, planned phases (from simulated fixtures), stop conditions, and policy summary into a single trace. `--save` persists to `.pcae/runner-simulations/latest.json`. Explicitly reports `would_execute=false` and `mutation_performed=false`. Blocked environment produces empty plan. 5 new tests.
- Runner Simulation Fixture Queue (Phase 72C): adds `pcae phase runner-sim-fixture`, `--json`, and `--count N` for generating deterministic simulated queue entries (SIM-001 through SIM-010) for runner planning tests. Entries are in-memory only; the real phase queue is never mutated. Count is clamped to 1-10. 5 new tests.
- Runner Stop-Condition Policy Matrix (Phase 72B): adds `pcae phase runner-policy` and `--json` exposing a documented stop-condition policy matrix for bounded runner behavior. Defines 16 conditions across 4 categories: hard stop (10), recoverable stop (2), advisory warning (3), and continue allowed (1). Task finish partial failure points to `pcae task finish recover`. Git lock issues point to `pcae doctor git-lock`. Human authority is explicitly stated as absolute. 4 new tests.
- Bounded Phase Runner Dry-Run Planner (Phase 72A): adds `pcae phase runner-plan`, `--json`, and `--max-phases N` for planning-only bounded runner computation. Shows planned phases from queue (capped at 3), stop conditions, validation sequence, commit/push sequence, and recovery path including `pcae task finish recover` and `pcae doctor git-lock`. Does not execute queue items, mutate queue, create tasks, or make commits. Empty queue reports no planned phases. Blocked environment reports blockers. 7 new tests.
- Phase Queue Runner Readiness Contract (Phase 71Z): adds `pcae phase runner-readiness` and `--json` for read-only three-tier readiness assessment. Reports `environment_ready` (clean tree, healthy, check passed, no active task, task memory clean), `queue_ready` (queue present and non-empty), and `runner_ready` (both environment and queue ready). Includes blocking reasons, advisory reasons, and full governance state. Does not execute queue items. 5 new tests.
- Autonomy Comparison Run Summary Artifact (Phase 71Y): adds `pcae phase autonomy-summary`, `--json`, and `--save` for read-only governance fact summaries useful for agent autonomy comparisons. Reports phases detected, warning count, latest completed phase, recovery command observations, active task, working tree, health, push status, latest handoff summary, and an agent-neutral note. `--save` persists to `.pcae/autonomy-summaries/latest.json` (auto-gitignored). Missing audit or handoff artifacts are handled gracefully. 5 new tests.
- Git Lock Diagnostic Visibility in Task Finish Failure (Phase 71X): when `pcae task finish --commit` fails during the closure commit with `.git/index.lock` or `Operation not permitted` errors, the output now includes actionable guidance: run `pcae doctor git-lock`, then `pcae task finish recover --dry-run`, then `pcae task finish recover --message "..."`. JSON output includes a `guidance` array with these commands. Normal commit failures without lock/permission errors remain unchanged. 3 new tests.
- Audit Handoff Summary Freshness (Phase 71W): `pcae phase audit-show --json` now includes `current_handoff_summary`, `current_handoff_created_at`, and `handoff_summary_stale` fields. When the latest handoff summary differs from the value captured at audit creation time, `handoff_summary_stale` is `true` and human output distinguishes "at audit" from "current" summaries. Existing `latest_handoff_summary` field preserved for backward compatibility. 4 new tests.
- Strategic Continuity Pointer Refresh (Phase 71V): bootstrap prompt now shows "Latest completed phase: <id>" derived from audit or handoff data. When the latest completed phase differs from the strategic lineage's activated phase, the strategic section is relabeled as "Historical strategic decision" to avoid implying it is the current next phase. Historical lineage remains visible for context. 7 new tests.
- Git Index Lock Permission Diagnostics (Phase 71U): adds `pcae doctor git-lock` and `--json` for read-only diagnosis of `.git/index.lock` issues. Reports whether a lock file exists, whether `.git` and `.git/index` are writable, and classifies the situation as `ok`, `lock_present_stale`, `lock_present_active_process`, or `permission_denied`. Each status includes a reason and suggested next action. No lock files are deleted or created. 5 new tests.
- Audit Commit Pair Classification Flexibility (Phase 71T): phase audit commit-pair recognition now accepts `Document`, `Design`, `Add`, and `Refine` verbs as valid implementation commit prefixes alongside `Implement`. Classification uses phase-id matching: any recognized verb followed by `Phase <id>` is treated as implementation unless the verb is `Complete` (which remains closure-only). Phases with documentation-only or design-only commits (e.g., `Document Phase 71S ...`) are no longer falsely warned as missing implementation commits. Warnings for genuinely missing implementation commits are preserved. 7 new tests.
- Codex Autonomy Comparison Handoff Note (Phase 71S): adds architecture documentation for agent-neutral autonomy comparison under PCAE governance. The note defines comparison criteria for Claude/Codex-style runs, expected end-of-run report fields, and the observed Codex 71Q/71Q.1/71R stop-and-recover behavior. It distinguishes agent governance behavior from the Codex sandbox `.git/index.lock` permission issue and reinforces that PCAE should provide governed recovery paths rather than relying on agent improvisation. Documentation only; no code behavior changes.
- Phase Prompt Queue Round-Trip Validation (Phase 71R): adds read-only `pcae phase prompt-roundtrip-check` and `--json` to validate captured prompt planning continuity without executing prompts or mutating prompt artifacts, queue state, or task contracts. The command checks latest prompt metadata/content, prompt-show loadability, prompt-enqueue dry-run derivation, readable phase queue state, planning-only queue-check boundary, and handoff/bootstrap visibility signals when artifacts exist. Missing prompt reports not ready with reasons. Existing queue entries are reported and never cleared.
- Partial Task Finish Recovery (Phase 71Q.1): adds `pcae task finish recover` with `--dry-run`, `--json`, and `--message`. The command detects the narrow post-failure state where task finish already moved exactly one task from `tasks/active/` to `tasks/done/` and updated `tasks/DONE.md`, but the closure commit failed. Recovery stages and commits only those closure files with `git commit --no-verify`; dry-run reports the plan without mutation; JSON reports task id, title, closure files, commit message, commit hash when committed, recovery status, and refusal reason. It refuses unrelated dirty files, ambiguous multiple transitions, active tasks, clean trees, and mismatched active/done filenames. Normal `pcae task finish --commit`, push behavior, task-memory doctor behavior, prompt handling, and queue behavior are unchanged.
- Phase Prompt Queue Metadata Preservation (Phase 71Q): phase queues now accept mixed legacy string entries and structured entries. `pcae phase prompt-enqueue` persists captured-prompt metadata (`title`, `source_type`, `source_prompt_path`, `source_prompt_created_at`, `created_at`) while manual `phase queue add` keeps writing string entries for backward compatibility. Queue list/check normalize titles for human output and expose metadata in JSON when available. Queue hygiene detects placeholder titles across both entry forms. Queue remains planning-only with no prompt execution or queue execution.
- Phase Prompt Queue Bridge Implementation (Phase 71P): adds `pcae phase prompt-enqueue` for safe planning-only bridge from captured phase prompts to the phase queue per 71O design. Enqueues latest prompt by default; `--file <filename>` enqueues a specific timestamped prompt. `--title` overrides queue item title. `--dry-run` reports without mutation. `--json` includes source path, created_at, title, queue length, and mutation status. Duplicate detection refuses entries already in queue. Missing prompt returns clear error. No prompt execution, no task creation, no queue execution. 10 new tests. Later Phase 71Q preserves source metadata in structured queue entries while keeping 71P string queues compatible.
- Phase Prompt Queue Bridge Design (Phase 71O): design document added to `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`. Defines `pcae phase prompt-enqueue latest|<filename>` command shape for transferring prompt title to phase queue entries. Metadata transfer model: title → queue description, path/created_at → informational source fields, content never transferred. Safety model: enqueue only, dry-run first, no execution, no automatic task creation, duplicate detection, multi-phase warning. Explains interaction with queue list/check, handoff/bootstrap visibility, audit artifacts, and future queue runner. No implementation — design only.
- Phase Prompt Hygiene (Phase 71N): adds `pcae phase prompt-hygiene` and `pcae phase prompt-prune` for managing phase prompt artifacts. `prompt-hygiene` detects placeholder-like prompts matching patterns: "test prompt", "placeholder", "dummy", "next step", "todo" (case-insensitive). `--clear-placeholders --confirm` removes only placeholder artifacts, preserving real prompts. `prompt-prune --keep N` retains newest N timestamped prompt artifacts, pruning older ones. `--dry-run` previews prune candidates. `latest.md`/`latest.json` are never touched by prune. Both commands support `--json`. 10 new tests.
- Phase Prompt Visibility in Bootstrap and Handoff (Phase 71M): handoff artifacts now include `prompt_summary` with `present`, `title`, `created_at`, and `path` fields when a captured phase prompt exists. `handoff-show` displays "Latest prompt:" line when present. Compact bootstrap shows "Latest prompt:" in the bootstrap prompt. `pcae session continuity-check` (human and `--json`) includes prompt presence, title, path, and created_at. No prompt mutation during any read surface. 9 new tests.
- Phase Prompt Show (Phase 71L): adds `pcae phase prompt-show` and `pcae phase prompt-list` for displaying captured phase prompts. `prompt-show` displays the latest captured prompt with title, created timestamp, and content. `prompt-show --json` includes all metadata plus content. Missing prompt returns clear error with nonzero exit. `prompt-list` lists timestamped prompt artifacts with count. Both commands are read-only. 8 new tests.
- Phase Prompt Capture (Phase 71K): adds `pcae phase prompt-capture` for saving phase prompts as local runtime artifacts. Supports `--text`, `--file`, and `--stdin` input sources. Creates timestamped artifact and updates `latest.md` and `latest.json` metadata. Artifacts stored in `.pcae/phase-prompts/` (gitignored). `--json` outputs capture metadata. Capture-only — does not execute prompts or create task contracts. Init template updated. 10 new tests.
- Post-Clear Continuity Validation (Phase 71J): adds `pcae session continuity-check` for read-only validation of post-clear/session-reset continuity state. Reports branch, working tree, health, check, task state, task memory, push mode, handoff artifact presence/status, audit artifact presence/status, phase queue presence/count, issues list, and whether repo is suitable for continuation. `--json` produces structured output. Exit code 0 when suitable, 1 when not. Command is strictly read-only. 9 new tests.
- Autonomy Audit Visibility in Handoff and Bootstrap (Phase 71I): handoff artifacts now include `audit_summary` with `present`, `created_at`, `phases_detected`, `warning_count`, and `healthy_idle` fields when a saved audit exists. `handoff-show` displays audit line when present. Compact bootstrap shows "Last audit:" line with phase count, warnings, and healthy idle status. No audit is generated or mutated during handoff or bootstrap. 8 new tests.
- Autonomy Audit Artifact Persistence (Phase 71H): `pcae phase audit --save` persists structured audit reports to `.pcae/phase-audits/latest.json` and timestamped `audit-<ts>.json`. `pcae phase audit-show` displays the latest saved audit (human and `--json`). Missing audit returns clear error with nonzero exit. Audit artifacts are gitignored. Init template updated. Existing audit behavior unchanged without `--save`. 10 new tests.
- Phase Queue Residue Hygiene (Phase 71G): adds `pcae phase queue hygiene` to detect and optionally clear placeholder/test queue entries. Detects entries matching patterns: "test phase", "next step", "placeholder", "dummy" (case-insensitive). `--json` reports findings and clearable count. `--clear-placeholders --confirm` removes only placeholder entries, preserving real queue entries. Without `--confirm`, clearing is refused. Clean queue reports no issues. 12 new tests.
- Governed Phase Queue Runner Design (Phase 71F): design document added to `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`. Refines Phase 70Z runner proposal with concrete specification leveraging 71C–71E infrastructure (`pcae phase audit`, queue visibility, `pcae phase queue check`). Defines `pcae phase queue run` command shape, governed one-phase-at-a-time execution sequence (16 steps), mandatory stop conditions (15 conditions), queue-run audit artifact shape, and external-agent-driven architecture. No implementation — design only.
- Phase Queue Readiness Check (Phase 71E): adds `pcae phase queue check` for read-only readiness validation before executing queued phases. Checks queue exists and is non-empty, working tree clean, health passes, pcae check passes, no active task, task memory clean, push not blocked. Reports `ready` or `not ready` with specific reasons. `--json` includes all readiness fields. 7 new tests.
- Phase Queue Visibility in Handoff and Bootstrap (Phase 71D): handoff artifacts now include `phase_queue_present`, `phase_queue_count`, and `phase_queue_next` fields. `handoff-show` displays queue status when present, silent when absent. Session bootstrap (both human and compact) surfaces queue state from handoff artifacts. No queue mutation during handoff or bootstrap. 8 new tests.
- Autonomy Batch Audit Report (Phase 71C): adds `pcae phase audit` for read-only audit reports on recent autonomous multi-phase runs. Detects implementation/completion commit pairs from git history, reports commit-pair completeness, current health/check/doctor/push state, latest handoff summary, and whether repo returned to healthy idle. Supports `--last N` (default 8), `--since PHASE_ID`, and `--json`. Warns on missing implementation or completion commits. 10 new tests.
- Push Readiness No-Op Semantics (Phase 71B): `pcae push check --json` now includes `push_blocked`, `push_action_required`, `push_noop`, and `push_reason` fields to distinguish benign no-op (`nothing_to_push`) from actual blocked state. `nothing_to_push` reports `push_blocked=false, push_noop=true`. Blocked state reports `push_blocked=true, push_action_required=true`. Existing `ready` field preserved for backward compatibility. 4 new tests.
- Bootstrap Handoff Freshness (Phase 71A): compact bootstrap now shows "Last handoff:" with summary, timestamp, latest commit, task state, review status, and next action when `.pcae/handoffs/latest.json` exists. The stale `PROJECT_STATUS.md` phase is demoted to "Phase (from PROJECT_STATUS.md):" when a handoff artifact provides newer context. Bootstrap without handoff artifact preserves existing behavior. `build_bootstrap_prompt` gains optional `handoff` parameter. 4 new tests.
- Governed Multi-Phase Runner Design (Phase 70Z): design document added to `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`. Proposes `pcae phase run-queue` with governed one-phase-at-a-time execution, mandatory stop conditions (test failure, health/check failure, scope drift, review enforcement), audit artifacts at `.pcae/phase-runs/`, and external-agent-driven architecture. No implementation — design only.
- Phase Queue Planning Command (Phase 70Y): adds `pcae phase queue add/list/show/clear` for advisory phase queue planning. Queue stored in `.pcae/phase-queue.json` (gitignored). Does not execute queued phases or create task contracts. All subcommands support `--json`. 10 new tests.
- Handoff Artifact Hygiene (Phase 70X): adds `pcae phase handoff-prune` to inspect and prune old timestamped handoff artifacts. `--keep N` specifies how many recent artifacts to retain (default: 20). `--dry-run` reports candidates without deleting. `--json` for machine-readable output. `latest.json` is never deleted. 7 new tests.
- Handoff Bootstrap Consumption (Phase 70W): `pcae session bootstrap` now reads and surfaces the latest handoff artifact from `.pcae/handoffs/latest.json` when available. Human output shows "Last handoff:" section with summary, branch, task state, health, check, push, review, latest commit, and next action. JSON output includes `latest_handoff` field (null when no artifact exists). Compact bootstrap `--json` also includes handoff data. Bootstrap does not mutate handoff artifacts. 6 new tests; existing bootstrap behavior preserved when no handoff exists.
- Handoff Artifact Persistence (Phase 70V): `pcae phase handoff` now persists structured handoff artifacts to `.pcae/handoffs/latest.json` and timestamped files. Artifacts include branch, working tree, task state, health, check, push readiness, lifecycle review, recent commits, and bootstrap command. `pcae phase handoff-show` displays the latest artifact (human and `--json`). Handoff directory is gitignored via `.pcae/.gitignore` and init template. JSON output includes all artifact fields alongside existing handoff data. 12 new tests; existing handoff behavior unchanged.
- Phase Handoff Auto-Summary (Phase 70U): `pcae phase handoff` now works with zero arguments. `--summary` is optional; when omitted, a concrete summary is auto-generated from branch, working tree, active task, health, check, unpushed commits, lifecycle review status, and latest commit. When `--summary` is provided, verbatim behavior is preserved. `--next-agent` defaults to the current lock holder when no `--next-agent` and no `--work-type` are provided. JSON output includes `auto_summary` boolean field. 11 new tests; existing handoff behavior unchanged.
- Policy-Controlled Lifecycle Review Enforcement (Phase 70T): adds `[lifecycle_review] require_approved = true` policy flag to make lifecycle review blocking at push readiness. Default behavior remains advisory. When enabled, `pcae push check` fails for `missing`, `changes_requested`, `informational_only`, `mixed`, and `unknown` review statuses; `approved` and `not_applicable` pass. `pcae push` refuses when policy-required review fails. JSON output includes `lifecycle_review_required`, `lifecycle_review_passed`, and `lifecycle_review_reason` fields. Human output shows `(required, passed)` or `(required, failed)` when enforcement is active. `parse_lifecycle_review_require_approved` added to policy parser. 10 new tests; existing advisory behavior unchanged.
- Lifecycle Automation (70A–70K): governed task lifecycle from creation through push. `pcae task finish --commit` validates, closes, and commits in one step. `pcae push` validates readiness and pushes. `pcae doctor task-memory --fix` repairs task-memory inconsistencies. Healthy idle state recognized when no active task exists with a clean working tree. Structured health status (`healthy_active`, `healthy_idle`, `unhealthy`) replaces string-based checks. Runtime session files (`.pcae/session.json`) are untracked by default.

- Implemented Execution Chain Traceability and Status Layer (Phase 69P): read-only observability over the full APA→ARA→EAR→ERR→ERRA→ECP→EPR→PER→RER artifact chain with zero artifact creation, modification, or deletion. `build_execution_chain_status(root, prompt_id)` walks all nine store layers and derives a single `chain_status` spanning `no_record` through `rolled_back` via `_ect_derive_chain_status`; each call re-reads from disk with no caching. `build_execution_chain_doctor(root, prompt_id=None)` runs five advisory-only diagnostic checks: dangling PER→EPR, dangling EPR→ECP, dangling RER→PER (all `severity="error"`), interrupted PER/RER (`in_progress` with no terminal successor, `severity="warning"`), and partial PER/RER (`severity="warning"`); findings never trigger repair, rollback, or re-execution. CLI surfaces: `pcae exec status --prompt-id <id> [--json]`; `pcae doctor execution-chain [--prompt-id <id>] [--json]`. `pcae approval-store show --prompt-id <id> [--json]` and `pcae approval-store list [--json]` expose APA store (via `lookup_approved_prompt_artifact`/`list_approved_prompt_artifacts`). `pcae authorization-store show --prompt-id <id> [--json]` and `pcae authorization-store list [--prompt-id <id>] [--json]` expose ARA store; `list_authorization_artifacts` extended with optional `prompt_id` filter parameter consistent with the filtering pattern of `list_promotion_reviews`, `list_promotion_execution_records`, `list_rollback_execution_records`. `--prompt-id` optional filter added to `promotion-review list`, `promotion-execution list`, and `rollback-execution list` CLI parsers, delegating to the existing `prompt_id` parameters on those list functions. `_ECT_GOVERNANCE_BOUNDARIES` (14 entries) encodes all mutation vectors as forbidden; static guard AST test confirms none of the six 69P read-only handlers calls any mutating function. Regression tests confirm `build_promotion_execution` and `build_rollback_execution` signatures unchanged; list functions retain prior keyword arguments. Design deviation: `authorization-store show` accepts `--prompt-id` (not `--authorization-id`) because the ARA store is keyed by prompt_id (`{prompt_id}-{ts}.json`) and no lookup-by-authorization_id function exists; documented in COMMANDS.md. `_ECT_PHASE_ID="69P"`. 49 `test_69p_*` tests; 5769 total tests passing.
- Transitioned active task from 69O Promotion Rollback Execution to 69P Execution Chain Traceability and Status Layer; session refreshed and governance continuity revalidated.
- Implemented Promotion Rollback Execution (Phase 69O): introduces RollbackExecutionRecord (RER, `.pcae/rollback-executions/`), the first PCAE artifact whose subject is reversing a root mutation, and `pcae rollback` the first command that does so. Internal identifiers use `_RER_*`/`_rer_*` -- checked against existing `_RREP_*`/`_ROLLBACK_*` design-level rollback-governance constants from earlier phases (50A-50K) before naming, no collision. Rollback is gated on a PromotionExecutionRecord (PER) with `status` in `{"completed", "partial"}` and `rollback_payload_available=True`; without that evidence rollback is refused outright (`per_status_not_eligible`, `rollback_payload_unavailable`) and no RER is created, mirroring how ECP/EPR gate failures in 69M/69N never persist anything. `file_plan` is derived strictly from `PER.file_results` where `outcome="success"` -- never user-specified, never including `already_applied` entries, since those were not written by the PER being rolled back (verified against the real 69N schema via `grep`/direct reads before writing any code, per explicit instruction). `_rer_check_divergence` inverts 69N's per-file hash check: a path whose current root hash matches the PER's `after_hash` is `pending` (still promoted, needs reverting); a path matching `before_hash` is `already_reverted` and is skipped without being re-written or treated as an error -- this is how re-running `pcae rollback` against the same PER resumes a partial rollback and is idempotent, with no `--resume` flag; a path matching neither is a `conflict` that blocks the entire attempt before any file is touched (`status="aborted_divergence"`, `file_results=[]`). For each file actually reverted: `before_exists=True` restores `before_content` (decoded from base64 if binary); `before_exists=False` removes the file -- this single rule correctly handles added/modified/deleted promotion entries uniformly without inspecting `change_type`. RER is created with `status="in_progress"` before the first restore and persisted after every file (same Condition-14-style never-silent principle as 69M/69N), so an interrupted rollback is always a stored, inspectable record; a second `pcae rollback` call against a PER with an `in_progress` RER is refused (`rollback_already_in_progress`). Partial rollback (mid-run write failure after divergence passed clean) is a valid terminal state, not automatically retried. `pcae rollback-execution mark-interrupted --rer-id <id>` transitions `in_progress` to `partial` as pure bookkeeping -- no file writes. `rollback_executed` is the first artifact where this field is dynamically `True` (only when this run actually restored/removed a file; `already_reverted` alone leaves it `False`). There is no mechanism to target an RER for reversal (`build_rollback_execution` takes only `per_id`, never `rer_id`), so rollback-of-rollback is forbidden by construction, not by a runtime check. `--dry-run` runs every gate and the divergence check without writing anything and without persisting an RER. CLI: `pcae rollback --per-id <id> [--dry-run]`, `pcae rollback-execution show/list/mark-interrupted`. Explicitly out of scope: `--override-divergence` consumption, multi-PER batch rollback, automatic rollback, git commit/push. 69N marked completed with successor 69O; 69O added as active in execution_governance_activation track with predecessor 69N; BR-005 current_phase advanced to 69O; capability "Promotion Rollback Execution" added to `_CRI_KNOWN_CAPABILITIES`/`_CI_KNOWN_CAPABILITIES`; `_SRG_CAPABILITY_OBJECTIVE_MAP` gains 71st entry; 69N prompt profiles changed from recommended to historical, 3 prompt profiles registered for 69O (recommended); SLR-69O-001 lineage record added (supersedes SLR-69N-001, decision_basis=roadmap_gap, 10 roadmap_debt entries); strategic lineage tests updated (current=SLR-69O-TEST, record_count=26, added `_valid_69o_record()`); `docs/COMMANDS.md`, `docs/ROADMAP_REGISTRY.md`, `docs/CAPABILITY_INVENTORY.md` regenerated; PROJECT_STATUS.md "Governed Root Mutation Achieved" milestone updated to reflect rollback no longer deferred; 52 new `test_69o_*` tests; 5720 total tests passing; execution_allowed=False always; rollback occurs only through the explicit `pcae rollback` human command.

- Implemented Write Promotion Execution (Phase 69N): introduces PromotionExecutionRecord (PER, `.pcae/promotion-executions/`), the first PCAE artifact and `pcae promote` the first command that mutates root. Internal identifiers use `_PXR_*`/`_pxr_*` (not `_PER_*`) to avoid colliding with the pre-existing Phase 45N `_PER_*` "Prompt Execution Readiness" constants discovered and fixed during implementation (`_PER_GOVERNANCE_BOUNDARIES` was being silently shadowed). Promotion is gated on an EPR with `promotion_authorized=True`, never on an ECP alone, via `build_promotion_execution(root, epr_id, dry_run=False)`. `_pxr_check_divergence` performs a per-file, resume-aware, content-hash divergence check (three-way: `pending` when current root hash matches ECP `before_hash`, `already_applied` when it matches `after_hash`, `conflict` otherwise or when the path is missing from the ECP or not `promotion_eligible`); git HEAD divergence alone is advisory only, never blocking. `already_applied` paths are skipped, never re-written, never treated as an error, recorded with `outcome="already_applied"` — this is how re-running `pcae promote` against the same EPR resumes a partial promotion, with no `--resume` flag and no additional authority expansion. Any per-file conflict blocks the entire attempt before any file is touched (`status="aborted_divergence"`); the EPR's `override_divergence` field from 69M is deliberately not consumed. PER is created with `status="in_progress"` and `file_results=[]` before the first file write and persisted after every file (mirrors the Condition 14 mandatory-attempt-never-silent principle from 69M), so an interrupted run is always a stored, inspectable record; a second `pcae promote` call against an EPR with an `in_progress` PER is refused (`promotion_already_in_progress`). Partial promotion (some files written, some failed after divergence passed clean — tested via a path that collides with an existing directory to force a write error) is a valid terminal state, not automatically retried. `pcae promotion-execution mark-interrupted --per-id <id>` transitions `in_progress` to `partial` as pure bookkeeping — no file writes, only valid from `in_progress`. `promotion_executed` is the first dynamic occurrence of a field that was a hardcoded `False` invariant on every prior artifact: `True` only when this run actually wrote a file (`already_applied` alone leaves it `False`). `rollback_payload_available` reports whether every successfully-written file had a captured `before_content`/`before_exists=False`; no rollback execution exists. Binary files are decoded from base64 before writing; deletions use `Path.unlink()`. `--dry-run` runs every gate and the divergence check without writing anything and without persisting a PER. CLI: `pcae promote --epr-id <id> [--dry-run]`, `pcae promotion-execution show/list/mark-interrupted`. Explicitly out of scope: rollback execution, git commit/push, automatic promotion, divergence-override consumption, multi-EPR batch promotion, atomic staged-rename writes (sequential write + incremental PER chosen as the smaller mechanism). 69M marked completed with successor 69N; 69N added as active in execution_governance_activation track with predecessor 69M; BR-005 current_phase advanced to 69N; capability "Write Promotion Execution" added to `_CRI_KNOWN_CAPABILITIES`/`_CI_KNOWN_CAPABILITIES`; `_SRG_CAPABILITY_OBJECTIVE_MAP` gains 70th entry; 69M prompt profiles changed from recommended to historical, 3 prompt profiles registered for 69N (recommended); SLR-69N-001 lineage record added (supersedes SLR-69M-001, decision_basis=roadmap_gap, 10 roadmap_debt entries); strategic lineage tests updated (current=SLR-69N-TEST, record_count=25, added `_valid_69n_record()`); `docs/COMMANDS.md`, `docs/ROADMAP_REGISTRY.md`, `docs/CAPABILITY_INVENTORY.md` regenerated; 60 new `test_69n_*` tests; 5668 total tests passing; execution_allowed=False always; root mutation occurs only through the explicit `pcae promote` human command.

- Implemented Write Governance Design (Phase 69M): introduces ExecutionChangePackage (ECP, `.pcae/execution-packages/`) and ExecutionPromotionReview (EPR, `.pcae/promotion-reviews/`) closing SLR-69L-004 (ECR captures paths not content). ECP is the canonical evidence artifact for sandbox-produced content: per-file `path`, `change_type`, `before_exists`/`after_exists`, `before_hash`/`after_hash` (SHA-256), `diff` (unified diff via `difflib`), `content`/`before_content` (text or base64 for binary), `binary`, `symlink`, `external_target`, `gitignored`, `promotion_eligible`, `exclusion_reason`; `manifest_hash` over all `after_hash` values; `git_head_diverged`/`git_commit_detected` derived from pre/post git HEAD. Condition 14 is the first post-execution governance condition: Conditions 1-13 are pre-execution (failure sets `execution_occurred=False`); Condition 14 evaluates after execution has already occurred inside the sandbox and cannot retroactively block it — ECP capture is a mandatory, ordering-enforced *attempt* inserted between post_state capture and `_esb_destroy_sandbox` in `invoke_readonly_execution`, but capture *success* is not mandated. Failure is never silent: a placeholder ECP is always stored (`capture_outcome="failed"`, partial `capture_errors`), surfaced as `execution_reviewable=False` on both ECP and ERR, rather than retroactively setting `execution_occurred=False`. A call-site try/except around `_ecp_capture` in `invoke_readonly_execution` provides defense in depth beyond `_ecp_capture`'s own internal try/except, guaranteeing sandbox destruction and ERR creation proceed regardless of ECP outcome (preserves ESB-C-003/004 cleanup guarantees from 69L). Hard exclusions (cannot be overridden by EPR): `.git/` (`git_directory_excluded`), `.pcae/` (`governance_directory_excluded`), external symlinks (`symlink_escape`). Default exclusions: toolchain prefixes (`toolchain_artifact_excluded`), gitignored files via batched `git check-ignore --stdin` (`gitignored`), oversized binaries over 1MB (`binary_size_threshold_exceeded`). `_ECP_GOVERNANCE_BOUNDARIES` includes `condition_14_category="post_execution"`, `post_execution_condition_cannot_retroactively_set_execution_occurred_false=True`, `post_execution_condition_failure_sets_reviewability_flag_not_blocker=True`, `ecp_capture_attempt_is_mandatory=True`, `ecp_capture_success_is_not_mandatory=True`, `automatic_promotion_allowed=False`, `production_containment_ready=False` (unchanged from 69L — observability is not containment). EPR (`build_promotion_review`) records a human's content-level review of a specific ECP, distinct from ERRA (execution-result review, not content review): `human_disposition` (approved/rejected/deferred/escalated/cancelled), partial-path approval (`approved_paths`/`rejected_paths`, `partial_approval` derived, `review_state="partial_approved"` when a proper subset of eligible paths is approved), `promotion_authorized` as a separate explicit flag from disposition (no promotion-execution consumer exists yet), `override_divergence`/`override_divergence_rationale`. EPR creation is blocked when the ECP is missing (`ecp_not_found`) or not `execution_reviewable` (`ecp_not_reviewable`); requesting approval of a non-`promotion_eligible` path is a hard validation error (`ineligible_paths_requested`), not a silent drop. `reviewed_by`/`reviewed_at` required only for terminal dispositions (approved/rejected/cancelled). `_EPR_GOVERNANCE_BOUNDARIES` includes `external_symlinks_not_approvable=True`, `pcae_directory_not_approvable=True`, `git_directory_not_approvable=True`, `automatic_approval_allowed=False`. CLI: `pcae execution-change-package show/list` (read-only — ECP can only be created automatically during sandboxed execution, never standalone, since the sandbox no longer exists by CLI invocation time); `pcae promotion-review create/show/list`. No promotion execution, no rollback execution, no git commit, no git push, no automatic promotion — all explicitly deferred to a future phase (69N). Accepted scope is ECP + EPR only. 69L marked completed with successor 69M; 69M added as active in execution_governance_activation track with predecessor 69L; BR-005 current_phase advanced to 69M; capability "Execution Change Package and Promotion Review" added to `_CRI_KNOWN_CAPABILITIES`/`_CI_KNOWN_CAPABILITIES`; `_SRG_CAPABILITY_OBJECTIVE_MAP` gains 69th entry; 69L prompt profiles changed from recommended to historical, 3 prompt profiles registered for 69M (recommended); SLR-69M-001 lineage record added (supersedes SLR-69L-001, decision_basis=roadmap_gap, 10 roadmap_debt entries covering ECP/EPR scope, hard exclusions, divergence detection, git-commit-in-sandbox detection, deferred promotion/rollback, and the Condition 14 mandatory-attempt mechanism — no separate SLR for the Condition 14 post-execution category label itself, which is documentation-only per explicit instruction); strategic lineage tests updated (current=SLR-69M-TEST, record_count=24, added `_valid_69m_record()`); `docs/COMMANDS.md`, `docs/ROADMAP_REGISTRY.md`, `docs/CAPABILITY_INVENTORY.md` regenerated; 58 new `test_69m_*` tests; 5608 total tests passing; execution_allowed=False and promotion_executed=False always; no root mutation in any ECP/EPR code path.

- Added Controlled Rollback Push (Phase 43E): `pcae remote rollback push JOB_ID` and `--json` push the rollback commit for an approved and executed rollback; push is gated on five conditions: `rollback_approval_state=="approved"`, `rollback_commit_sha` present on the job, `rollback_status` in `("rolled_back", "already_rolled_back")`, clean working tree, and rollback commit reachable from HEAD via `_check_commit_is_ancestor`; on success, `rollback_pushed_at`, `rollback_push_status="pushed"`, and `rollback_remote_branch` are persisted on the job file; JSON output includes `pushed`, `job_id`, `rollback_commit_sha`, `remote_branch`, `push_status`, `advisory`; human output shows Rollback Push header, rollback approval state, rollback commit SHA, push status, remote branch, and advisory; pending/denied approval, missing rollback commit SHA, invalid rollback status, dirty working tree, and unreachable rollback commit all exit 1 with clear messages; git push timeout exits 1; `already_rolled_back` status is accepted for push (idempotent rollback can still be pushed); no new rollback commit is created; `push_rollback`, `ROLLBACK_PUSH_ADVISORY`, `_ROLLBACK_EXECUTED_STATUSES` added to `core/agent.py`; `run_remote_rollback_push` added to `commands/agent.py`; `push JOB_ID [--json]` subcommand wired under `remote rollback` in `cli.py`; advisory: "Rollback push completed through PCAE governance."; 14 new tests.

- Fixed Rollback Result Consistency (Phase 43D.1): `pcae remote rollback execute JOB_ID` is now idempotent; if `rollback_commit_sha` is already recorded on the job, the command returns `rollback_status="already_rolled_back"` with `rolled_back=true` and `exit_code=0` without running `git revert` again; this eliminates the observed split where the first call reported `rolled_back` but a second call emitted `Rollback failed ... git revert exited 1` (because git revert on an already-reverted commit exits 1); JSON and human outputs now always agree — success reports `rolled_back`, repeated execution reports `already_rolled_back`, failure reports the error; `rollback_commit_sha` is preserved from the first execution and never overwritten; no approval state is mutated; no push, reset, or commit deletion occurs; change is a single early-return guard in `execute_rollback` in `core/agent.py`; 6 new tests covering: second execute returns `already_rolled_back`, SHA preserved, no duplicate `git revert` call, required JSON fields on idempotent return, first success emits no failure message, and human/JSON agreement across both invocations.
